He is called mighty because he came to overcome the powers of the air. Hence the Psalmist says: “The Lord is strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle” (Ps. 23). Descending—that is, humbling himself by the assumption of humanity—from heaven, that is, from the knowledge of angels, [Col. 0356A] or because he made himself knowable to humankind. His descent was the humility of the Incarnation. Clothed with a cloud, namely concealed in flesh, which is refreshment for us against vices; and a rainbow upon his head, because “God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself” (2 Cor. 5). The Lord ascended upon a light cloud when he assumed flesh without the weight of sin. And his face was like the sun: that is, the knowledge which believers have of him is clear like the sun, because one who has true knowledge of him believes him to be God. Thus the face of the angel signifies the Incarnation of the Son of God, through which we have knowledge of him. Hence the Psalmist says: “Show us, O Lord, your face, and we shall be saved” (Ps. 79). And his feet were like pillars of fire. The Lord’s feet are believers [Col. 0356B] strong in faith, kindled by divine fire, and sustaining others as a pillar does.

### Verse 2

And he had in his hand an open little book: namely all the Scriptures fulfilled by his work, partly by preaching, partly by accomplishing what had been said concerning himself, and finally by opening their meaning to his disciples. His hand is the work of our salvation. And he placed his right foot—that is, the stronger preachers—upon the sea, that is, upon the greater and more overflowing tribulations of this present age; but his left foot—that is, those less strong in enduring evils and less active in doing good—he sends upon the earth, namely among less overwhelming tribulations. And the angel himself [Col. 0356C] acts through these same greater and lesser preachers.

### Verse 3

And he cried with a loud voice, namely concerning great matters, yet terribly, as a lion roars. The lion’s voice displays its strength and brings terror. And when he had cried—namely, because those sent by him had preached—the seven thunders spoke: that is, all their successors, bringing terror and uttering voices suited to their times. He terrifies when he says: “Every tree that does not bear good fruit shall be cut down and cast into the fire” (Matt. 3).

### Verse 4

And I was about to write what the seven thunders had spoken. Here he bears the person of those who, in the time of Antichrist, will wish to preach in imitation of the preceding [Col. 0356D] Fathers. And I heard a voice from heaven—that is, divine inspiration or angelic admonition—saying, that is, explaining, “Seal”—that is, make secret—what the seven thunders have spoken, so that it may be evident to friends and hidden from enemies; and do not write it, that is, do not reveal it to unbelievers, among whom these things have no place. As though he said plainly: O preachers of the Church, do not cast pearls before swine (Matt. 7).

### Verse 5

And the angel whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth lifted his hand to heaven and swore by him who lives for ages of ages. As though he said: Christ lifted up—that is, exalted—his hand, namely his humanity, to heaven, through which God the Word united to himself was working, as by a hand; and he swore—that is, confirmed it—through himself, exalted, and through God his Father, who lives for ages of ages.

### Verse 6

Who created heaven and the things in it, and earth and the things upon it, and sea and the things in it: because time, namely change—now night, now day, now prosperity, now adversity, now death, now life—will be no more for his faithful, because they will become immortal and incapable of suffering in eternal blessedness; whereas the time of the wicked lasts for ages. For the righteous there shall be no time—that is, no change—because they will be unchangeable in mind and incorruptible in body. Time is the succession of days and nights; therefore there will be no time there [Col. 0357B] where no variation of any thing will appear, but abiding brightness and unfailing light will always remain with them.

### Verse 7

But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he begins to sound the trumpet—that is, when he begins to preach—it will not be delayed, but the mystery of God will immediately be completed, that is, fulfilled: namely, the reward of the saints. This mystery is secret, because “eye has not seen, nor ear heard, what God has prepared for those who love him” (Isa. 64). As he announced through his servants the prophets; for the prophets’ first purpose was the coming of the Lord, and their second the consummation of the age. Therefore, after the destruction which shall occur in the time [Col. 0357C] of Antichrist had been shown, and after preaching had even been withdrawn because of it, and consolation supplied to the faithful for this purpose, he is commanded to preach what he saw. It is as though it were said to him openly: Behold, I have revealed everything to you; now go and preach. Do not be afraid because these things are harsh, nor be terrified by any tribulation, because you will not suffer as much as those who persevere in the time of Antichrist will suffer. This is placed here for the consolation of the present Church, where a greater tribulation is foretold.

### Verse 8

And I heard a voice—that is, divine admonition—from heaven, speaking again with me about the same matters and giving, namely, explanations. As though it said more plainly: O John, because the mystery of this momentary persecution and reward will soon be completed, go and take the open book from the angel’s hand: that is, preach to the children of the Church what you have heard and seen. As though he said openly: Go by the steps of virtues, deserve God’s grace, and through it understand, because he will reveal everything to you. Take the open book, namely that of the Gospel—that is, Scripture fulfilled by God and shown to believers—from the hand of the angel, namely through Christ’s work, standing upon sea and earth, ready to help those who approach him.

### Verse 9

And I went to the angel, asking him to give me the book. And he said to me: “Take it and devour it.” As though he said plainly: I enlarged my mind and went to the angel in obedience, leaving all that I had, asking him to give me the book—that is, understanding of the Scriptures. The action of the saints most readily follows the Lord’s commanding voice through prayer and work [perhaps “assembly,” *coetus*]. And because, when God sees someone ready, he freely offers what is necessary, the angel said to me: Take the book, incorporate it into yourself, and devour it—that is, work through it by inquiry and action, and distribute it to others. Yet because fulfilling it is burdensome to human nature, which is weak and fragile, it will make your stomach bitter; but in your mouth—that is, in your more perfect disciples through whom you speak—it will be sweet as honey in contemplation and preaching.

### Verse 10

And I took the book from the angel’s hand—that is, by following Christ’s work—and devoured it, and my stomach was made bitter. We have holy preachers who meditate day and night upon the law of the Lord and can say with the Psalmist: “How sweet are your words to my palate, more than honey to my mouth” (Ps. 118). And when I had taken the book, although I experienced bitter things, he nevertheless warned me not to cease preaching through fear of death, saying to me: You shall depart from prison, namely from the island of Patmos.

### Verse 11

You must again prophesy to peoples, nations, languages, and many kings.

## Chapter 11

### Verse 1

And a reed was given to me, namely Scripture written with a reed, like a rod—that is, a scepter—because it establishes kings. Kings carry a rod in their hand as a sign of their power, and by it their royal [Col. 0358C] authority is expressed. Therefore the reed—that is, divine Scripture—is compared to a rod, because it promises a kingdom to those who observe it, saying: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” (Matt. 5). A reed like a rod was given to me, saying: “Rise,” that is, rise up to preach, “and measure the temple of God,” namely preach according to each person’s capacity; “and the altar,” namely establish the Church and within it the altar; “and those who worship in it,” that is, establish how the faithful are to worship God in spirit and truth. The altar in the temple signifies the more eminent faithful in the Church: namely virgins who are continent and renounce the world, in whom the unceasing and unfailing fire of holy compunction especially remains.

### Verse 2

But cast out the court which is outside the temple—that is, false Christians, who pretend to be the Church but deny it by their deeds—by excommunicating them, namely show that they are outside; and do not measure it, that is, completely withdraw preaching from it, because it has been given to the Gentiles—that is, they have become like Gentiles, worshiping idols, and thus will perish with them in the common punishment. And they who are the courts—that is, heretics, pagans, Jews, and false Christians—will tread down, namely persecute, the holy city, that is, the Church assembled for good living and fortified with virtues, for forty-two months, that is, for the three and a half years in which Antichrist will reign. As though he said more plainly: Know that all persecutions occurring at present and [Col. 0359A] those occurring in the past proceed from Antichrist, just as will those which occur in his own time.

As [Note: [Col. 0359D] Everything which Martin adduces concerning Antichrist is transcribed from the book *On the Life of Antichrist*, circulated under the names of Augustine, Alcuin, and Rabanus; but the Benedictines, vol. XI, in the Appendix on additions and corrections to vol. VI of St Augustine, judge it to be the work of Adso, abbot of the monastery of Derbensis, in the time of Louis d’Outremer, king of the Franks.] our authorities say, Antichrist will be born from the people of the Jews, namely from the tribe of Dan, according to the prophecy which says: “Let Dan be a serpent in the way, a horned serpent in the path” (Gen. 49). For this reason he will sit in the way and be in the path: that he may strike those who walk in the paths of righteousness and kill them with the poison of his malice. He will be born through the intercourse of father and mother, but he will be conceived wholly in sin, generated in sin, and born in sin. At the very beginning of his conception, moreover, the devil will enter his mother’s womb together with him; and he will be nourished and protected in her womb by the devil’s malignity. And just as the Holy Spirit came upon the mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 0359B] overshadowed her with his power, and filled her with divinity, so that she might conceive of the Holy Spirit and what would be born might be divine and holy (Luke 1), so the devil will descend into the womb of Antichrist’s mother, fill her entirely, surround her entirely, hold her entirely, and possess her wholly inwardly and outwardly, so that, with the devil’s cooperation, she may conceive through a human being and what is born may be wholly wicked, wholly malicious, and damned. Hence that man is called “the son of perdition” (2 Thess. 2), because, insofar as he can, he will destroy the human race, and he himself will finally be destroyed. He will be born in Babylon. The apostle Paul says that Antichrist will not come into the world until the apostasy first comes: that is, until all kingdoms formerly subject to the Roman Empire first fall away from it. But this time has not yet come, because although we see that the Roman Empire has been destroyed for the most part, nevertheless, so long as the kings of the Franks endure, who ought to hold the Roman Empire, the dignity of the Roman kingdom will not utterly perish, because it will stand in its kings. Therefore it means only this, as the Apostle says: “Let him who now holds, hold until he is removed from the midst” (ibid.). “As [Note: [Col. 0360D] *The City of God*, book XX, chapter 19, section 3.] blessed Augustine says, this is not implausibly believed to have been said concerning the Roman Empire itself. It is as though he said: Let him who now rules continue to rule until he is removed from the midst—that is, taken away from the midst—and then that wicked one will be revealed” (ibid.), “whom no one doubts is signified as Antichrist.”

[Col. 0359D] Some of our teachers, however, say that one of the kings of the Franks will hold the Roman Empire in its entirety, because he will exist in the last time, and he will be the greatest and the last of all kings. After he has governed his kingdom prosperously, he will finally go to Jerusalem and willingly lay down his scepter and crown upon the Mount of Olives. This will be the end and consummation of the Roman and Christian empire. Immediately thereafter, according to the Apostle’s statement, [Col. 0360A] they say Antichrist will appear. Then Antichrist will be revealed. Although he is a human being, he will nevertheless be the source of all sins and the son of perdition—that is, of the devil—not by nature but by imitation. For he will fulfill the devil’s will in every respect, because the fullness of diabolical power and of every evil device will dwell bodily in him, in whom all the treasures of malice and iniquity will be hidden (Col. 2). He, therefore, as we said above, born in the city of Babylon, will come to Jerusalem and circumcise himself, saying to the Jews: “I am the Christ promised to you, who has come for your salvation, in order that I may gather and defend you from every land.” Then all the Jews will flock to him, thinking that they are receiving God, but they will receive the devil.

[Col. 0360B] But lest Antichrist deceive and destroy the whole world, two great prophets will be sent into the world, namely Enoch and Elijah. They will fortify and instruct God’s faithful against Antichrist’s assault with divine weapons, teaching and preaching for three and a half years. Whatever children of Israel are found at that time, these two greatest teachers and prophets will convert them to Christ’s faith and make them, among the elect, inseparable from the pressure of so great a storm, as Scripture says: “Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of it shall be saved” (Isa. 10). Therefore, after they have completed their preaching for three and a half years, Antichrist’s persecution will immediately begin to blaze, and he will first take up his weapons against them and kill them. [Col. 0360C] After these two have been killed, he will persecute the rest, making some glorious martyrs and others apostates; and whoever believes in him will receive the mark of his character.

Therefore this Antichrist, artificer of all wickedness, after he has afflicted the entire world for three and a half years, tortured all God’s people with different punishments, killed Elijah and Enoch, and crowned with martyrdom the others who persevere in the faith, will finally be met by God’s judgment. As blessed Paul writes, saying: “Whom the Lord Jesus, by the power of his command, [Note: [Col. 0360D] The corrupt passage should be restored thus: “Whom the Lord will kill with the breath of his mouth”; or “the Lord Jesus will kill him by the power of his command” (Benedictine edition: “vision”; manuscript of Adso: “power”), or else the archangel, etc.],” or whom the archangel Michael will kill, he will be slain through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ. Our elders [Col. 0360D] and teachers also hand down that Antichrist will be killed on the Mount of Olives, in his pavilion and upon his throne, in that place where the Lord ascended into heaven. Of him the prophet says: “The Lord will cast down the illustrious one of the whole earth upon the holy mountain” (Lam. 2), that is, upon the Mount of Olives.

Moreover, dearest brothers, you ought to know that after Antichrist has been killed, the day of the Lord’s judgment will not come immediately. Rather, as is read in the book of Daniel, [Col. 0361A] the Lord will grant forty [Note: [Col. 0361D] Alcuin and the manuscript of Adso likewise have “forty,” but the parallel Gloss more correctly gives “forty-five,” for here the author of the book alludes to Daniel’s passage: “Blessed is he who waits and reaches the thousand three hundred and thirty-five days” [Dan. 12:12]. For forty-five added to the 1,290 of the preceding verse makes a total of 1,335. For explanation of this passage, see the interpreters.] days to the elect who were deceived by Antichrist, so that they may repent (Dan. 12). But after they have performed this repentance, how much time or interval will pass until the Lord comes for judgment, no one knows; but, as he himself says in the Gospel, it remains in God’s ordering (Mark 13). But let us hear what the angel, speaking in the person of the Lord, says concerning the two great prophets.

VERS. 3.—“I will give [power] to my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy,” that is, preach, “for one thousand two hundred and sixty days,” namely for three and a half years, as Jesus Christ preached, “clothed in sackcloth,” that is, preaching repentance and showing it by their example, like John the Baptist, who was clothed in camel’s hair [Col. 0361B] (Matt. III). Or, because the life of the saints will seem contemptible to the reprobate, they are therefore said to come to preach clad in sackcloth. This concerns Elijah and Enoch, through whom many other preachers are understood. The Church is fittingly represented in two witnesses, on account of the two Testaments; or because it consists of two peoples; or on account of the two kinds of martyrdom; or on account of the love of God and neighbour. In their praise he again adds, saying:

VERS. 4.—“These are the two olive trees,” namely anointed by the Holy Spirit, “and the two lampstands,” enlightening others, “standing before the Lord of the earth,” that is, attending to what pleases the Lord; or because they have been translated into Paradise, where Adam was once, and removed from our sight, they enjoy the brightness of the vision of God.

[Col. 0361C] VERS. 5.—“And if anyone wishes to harm them,” namely to recall them from their holy purpose, “fire,” that is, a spiritual sentence, “will go out from their mouth”; this will be to some “an aroma of life unto life,” to others “an aroma of death unto death” (II Cor. II), “and will devour,” that is, condemn, “their enemies.” “And if anyone wishes to injure them” by bodily death, “thus,” namely by a spiritual sentence, “he must be killed.”

VERS. 6.—“These have power to shut heaven,” that is, the Scriptures which conceal mysteries, “so that it may not rain during the days of their prophecy,” because they will not preach except at a fitting time. Likewise, all preachers of the Church are signified and comprehended in these two prophets, who received the Holy Spirit at the time of baptism and of the bishops’ laying on of hands [Col. 0361D]. For all teachers ought to imitate them. These two prophets also “have power over the waters,” that is, over their teachings, which are waters refreshing the faithful, “to turn them into blood,” namely into mortification; for their preaching will be to some unto life, to others unto death; “and to strike the earth with every plague,” that is, earthly persons, “as often as they will,” just as Moses turned the waters of the Nile into blood (Exod. IV, 7), and Elijah shut heaven so that it did not rain for three and a half years (III Kings XVII).

[Col. 0362A] VERS. 7.—“And when they have finished their testimony, the beast,” that is, Antichrist, “which ascends to kingship from the abyss,” namely from the hidden judgment of God, since “the judgments of the Lord are a great abyss” (Ps. XXXV); or it ascends from hell, because, just as “all the fullness of divinity dwells bodily” in Christ (Col. II), so all the fullness of wickedness dwells bodily in Antichrist. “And it shall make war against them” by false disputations, “and shall overcome them.” He does not say, “shall overcome them,” because they will ever be recalled from their purpose; but “shall overcome,” that is, shall kill them bodily.

VERS. 8.—“And their bodies shall lie in the streets of the great city,” namely Jerusalem, which was once great in virtues and will then be great in wickedness; so that whoever sees them lying dead may fear to conform himself to them [Col. 0362B] and to bury them. This city “will be called spiritually Sodom,” that is, mute, because no one there will dare to preach faith in the Holy Trinity; “and Egypt,” namely dark, without the knowledge of God. Or it will be called Sodom because of the deeds of the Sodomites, “where also their Lord was crucified.” Although persecution will rage everywhere, the Church’s affliction will nevertheless be greater and harsher where the Lord was crucified and where Antichrist, the head of all evils, will appear. The bodies of the saints are especially said to lie in its street, as though, where the chief conflict will be, there the unburied bodies of the dead will lie in great numbers. It is also understood from this that the Jewish people will adhere especially to Antichrist, until those among them who are to be saved return to Christ through the preaching of Elijah and Enoch [Col. 0362C]. By the great city Jerusalem, in which their bodies shall lie, the whole world is understood, because at that time saints will be killed in every part of the world. It follows:

VERS. 9.—“And some from peoples and tribes and tongues and nations shall see,” some with their eyes and some by report, “their bodies for three and a half days,” that is, for three and a half years; “and they shall not allow their bodies to be laid in tombs,” namely lest their memory endure and their tombs be venerated.

VERS. 10.—“And those who dwell upon the earth,” that is, those adhering to earthly things, “shall rejoice and make merry over” [Col. 0362D] “them”; they will arrange entertainments and play together for joy, and send gifts to one another. This is because these two prophets tormented those who dwell upon the earth by reproving their wickedness. For the Lord’s suffering outside the gate of the city (Heb. XIII) signified that he would suffer in his members throughout the whole world.

VERS. 11.—“And after three days,” that is, after three and a half years, “the Spirit of life from God entered into them”: namely, their souls, sent from God, eternally bestowing immortality and impassibility upon them, will enter into them [Col. 0363A]. And now impassible and immortal, “they stood,” that is, shall stand, “upon their feet,” that is, upon themselves, as they had previously been, needing nothing upon which to lean; and “great fear,” namely the punishment of hell or reverence for God, “fell,” that is, shall fall as a crushing weight, “upon those who saw,” that is, shall see, them thus glorified.

VERS. 12.—“And they heard,” that is, shall hear, “a great voice,” namely a voice of great power, “from heaven,” that is, from Christ or from an archangel, saying to them: “Come up here,” namely into the fellowship of the saints. “And they ascended,” that is, shall ascend, “into heaven,” and this “in a cloud,” which will refresh them and terrify their enemies; and “their enemies saw,” that is, shall see, them thus honoured—those whom here they regarded as foolish and insane [Col. 0363B].

[Note: [Col. 0363D] Augustine, *The City of God*, book XX, chapter 20.] If anyone, considering Paul’s statement, asks how the sentence pronounced generally upon the first man is fulfilled, when God said to him, “You are earth, and into earth you shall go” (Gen. III), he should know that both God’s and Paul’s statement are true. For living people will indeed be found, in whose person the Apostle speaks thus; and yet, as blessed Augustine says, in that very rapture into the clouds they will nevertheless taste a momentary death. Therefore they will return to earth; for the body’s returning to earth means that, when the soul departs, the body remains—which is certainly earth. Thus we confidently say that, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, in the very clouds, those who are found alive at the Lord’s coming will receive the Spirit of life. As has been said, they will both taste a momentary death [Col. 0363C] and return to earth. The wicked indeed will be cast down into hell, but the elect will be raised in the clouds to glory (I Cor. XV). Therefore the unrighteous and all their enemies will see them, and will perceive as just judges those whom they judged and condemned unjustly.

VERS. 13.—“And in that hour,” of the killing or glorification of these two prophets, namely Enoch and Elijah, “there was a great earthquake”; that is, earthly persons were moved toward the destruction of the Church when its teachers had been killed. “And a tenth part of the city fell”: that is, all the wicked fell away from the Church into punishments, or were utterly destroyed in hell. “And there were killed in the earthquake” those, namely, who afterwards did not withdraw from their evils through repentance [Col. 0363D], “seven thousand names of men”: that is, all perfected in wickedness, whom God foreknew unto death, lest even the faithful should be terrified in any way. “And the rest,” namely the good, who did not fall into punishment or sin, “were put in fear,” that is, they fear in reverence for God lest they fall, attributing nothing to themselves; “and they gave glory to the God of heaven.”

VERS. 14.—“The second woe has gone; and behold, the third woe comes quickly.”

VERS. 15.—“And the seventh angel,” in the order of narration and of time, “sounded the trumpet; and there were great voices in heaven,” that is, praises to God for the salvation of the righteous [Col. 0364A] and the condemnation of the wicked, saying: “The kingdom of our God and of his Christ has come”: he who was previously rejected now reigns, crowning the good and condemning the wicked; “and he shall reign,” that is, his kingdom shall remain, “for ever and ever. Amen.”

VERS. 16.—“And the twenty-four elders”: that is, not only the lesser faithful will glorify God in this way, but also the greater, who “sit in the sight of God,” that is, judge what is present, considering what pleases God, “on their thrones,” namely those entrusted to them; “they fell,” that is, humbled themselves, “upon their faces,” namely into their hearts, “and worshipped God,” that he might preserve them, saying:

VERS. 17.—“We give thanks to you, Lord God Almighty,” namely because you have saved us and condemned [Col. 0364B] our enemies; “who are” unchangeable, “and who were,” long ago when you were despised by the Jews; “who have taken” by rising again “your great power,” that is, by giving the Holy Spirit to your own and gathering the Church; “and have reigned,” namely by defending us from the devil.

VERS. 18.—“And the nations were angry at your kingdom.” Hence the Psalmist says: “The Lord reigns; let the peoples be angry. You who sit upon the cherubim, let the earth be moved” (Ps. XCVIII). “And your wrath came against them,” that is, the time of your vengeance; and “the time came,” namely the fitting occasion, “for the dead to be judged,” both good and evil, so that the good may be separated from the evil; and the time came “to give reward to your servants the prophets,” that is, to the other foreknowing ones, “and to the saints,” namely those established in faith, “and to those who fear your name, small” [Col. 0364C] “and great,” that is, not only the greater but all the faithful; and the time came “to destroy those who corrupted the earth,” that is, themselves through evil action and others through evil example.

VERS. 19.—“And the temple of God was opened in heaven, and the ark of his covenant was seen in his temple.” It should be noted that these past tenses are used for future events: “the temple was opened,” “the ark of the covenant was seen,” and “a sign appeared in heaven.” It is as if he said: On the day of judgment it will be revealed that the temple of God was in heaven; and then it will also be seen that the ark [perhaps *arcam*, “the ark”] of the covenant was in his temple, and why lightnings occurred; and the great sign which was previously unknown to many will appear, etc. Therefore the temple of God was opened in heaven: namely Christ, who is the temple of God, in whom “all the fullness of divinity dwells bodily” (Col. II), came to the knowledge of the Church, which has its spiritual manner of life in heavenly things. “And the ark of his covenant,” namely of God the Father, “was seen”: that is, this same Christ, who contains in himself the mystery of God the Father, just as the ark of the covenant contained the Old Testament. For he himself bore witness to all that he heard from his Father; he himself is our spiritual food and refreshment, signified by the manna hidden in the ark; he himself is our king and priest, signified by Aaron’s rod, which was kept [Col. 0365A] in the ark. “And there were lightnings,” that is, miracles which strike terror into those who see them; “and thunders,” namely preachings threatening eternal death to sinners; “and great hail,” namely preaching that proclaims God’s wrath, which crushes and punishes those unwilling to turn; “and an earthquake”: all earthly persons were moved, some toward faith and some toward persecution.

## CHAPTER XII

VERS. 1–2.—“And after these things a great sign was seen in heaven”: namely, “a woman clothed with the sun,” signifying the holy Church, which is clothed, covered, and defended on every side by Jesus Christ, her bridegroom and protector, who is the true sun of righteousness (Mal. IV); “and the moon beneath her feet,” because the holy Church despises and counts as nothing all earthly things, which wax and wane like the moon, as mud which she tramples beneath her feet. “And on the head of the same woman was a crown of twelve stars,” that is, Christ, who is the head and ruler of the whole Church, surrounded and crowned by the twelve apostles, who shine like stars in the Church. And the woman, that is, the holy Church, has the word of God in her womb, namely in the secret place of her mind, “and was pregnant,” that is, filled with the word of God; and “in labour,” desiring to bring forth many faithful people for Christ and make them conformed to him. “She cried out,” namely seeking help from the Lord with great intensity of heart; and “was tormented,” that is, endured many torments and labours, that she might bring forth, namely that through faith she might acquire many children for God [Col. 0365C]. Hence blessed Paul says: “My little children, for whom I am again in labour until Christ is formed in you” (Gal. IV). Blessed John again adds:

VERS. 3.—“Another sign was seen in heaven; and behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns.” As if he said: Besides the things stated above, another sign was seen by me: namely a great red dragon, signifying the devil, who is strong in wickedness and red, that is, bloodthirsty, by spiritually killing human beings; having in his power seven heads, namely all the rulers of the world, and ten horns, namely all those subject to the rulers of the earth, through whom those rulers attack and persecute those who keep the ten commandments of the law. “And upon the heads of the dragon,” that is, upon the rulers of the earth who obey him, “were seven diadems,” that is, victories over all who are given over to perdition [Col. 0365D].

VERS. 4.—“And his tail,” that is, his hidden deception, “drew to itself a third part of the stars of heaven,” namely those who seemed to shine in the Church with virtues like stars, “and cast them down to earth”: those, namely, whom it drew to itself, it entangled in the love and desire of earthly things. As was said, the woman cried out in labour, and the dragon, that is, the devil, strong in wickedness and powerful in iniquity, “stood before the woman,” that is, persevered in warfare against the Church, which was about to bring forth—namely, to call people to faith and make them conformed to Christ. Therefore the dragon [Col. 0366A], that is, the devil, stood before the woman, so that when she had brought forth a son—that is, when the Church had made some Christian like herself—he might devour him: namely, might by the craft of his malice recall him from the faith and incorporate him into himself. Thus the dragon, that is, the devil, was ready to devour the woman’s son, but could not, because the holy Church

VERS. 5.—“Brought forth a male child,” that is, Christ, strong and unconquerable, of whom it was said: “Behold, the man whose name is the East” (Zech. VI). He “was to rule,” that is, was to govern and defend, “all nations with a rod of iron,” namely through inflexible and upright justice. “And her son,” namely God and man, Jesus Christ, “was caught up to God,” that is, exalted to the right hand of God the Father, “and to his throne,” even to his own judicial seat, from which he judges all things with the Father [Col. 0366B].

VERS. 6.—“And the woman,” that is, the holy Church, “fled into the wilderness”: she left behind earthly dignity and the tumult of the world. In this wilderness she has a place prepared by God, namely quietness of mind, so that there he may feed her with the bread of the heavenly word for “one thousand two hundred and sixty days,” that is, for three and a half years; because for so many years the Son of God and of the Virgin himself preached.

VERS. 7.—“And there was a battle in heaven,” that is, in the Church and on behalf of the Church: Michael, whose name is interpreted “Who is like God?”, and his angels fought with the dragon; and the dragon fought with Michael and [Col. 0366C] his angels.

VERS. 8.—“And they did not prevail”: that is, the dragon and his angels had no strength in that battle; “nor was their place found any longer in heaven,” that is, in the Church.

VERS. 9.—“And that great dragon,” that is, the devil who cast down the first man, “was cast out,” namely far from the Church; he “was called the devil,” that is, one flowing downward, “and Satan,” namely the adversary, who “deceives,” that is, leads away from the right path, not only the first parent but also the whole world.

VERS. 10.—“And I heard a great voice in heaven,” that is, a certain exultation in the Church, namely [Col. 0366D] an angelic voice, saying: Before Christ’s coming the devil was prince of this world; but now salvation has come, that is, the healing of the ancient wound; and strength, namely the power to resist and conquer the devil; and the kingdom of our God—now, namely, our God, the Trinity, has a kingdom on earth, now he rules his Church; and the authority of his Christ—namely, according to his humanity, all authority in heaven and earth has been given to Christ, his Son. And this is because “the accuser of our brethren,” that is, the devil, who makes our brethren liable to accusation, “has been cast out,” namely removed far from God’s servants; he who “by day and by night,” that is, continually, or in prosperity and adversity, accused them before the Lord, namely made them liable to accusation and guilty. And [Col. 0367A], although the children of the Church were thus assailed by the devil, nevertheless

VERS. 11.—“They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb,” that is, by the shedding of Christ’s blood, this being the cause, and “by the word of their testimony,” namely their preaching which bore witness to Christ; and therefore they overcame him. They also overcame him for this reason: “they did not love their souls,” that is, their carnal pleasures, “even unto death”; namely, they did not use temporal goods for excess, but for necessity. Now the angels direct their discourse to the faithful who conquered the devil, saying:

VERS. 12.—“Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them.” As if they said: O you heavens, namely you who excel more greatly in virtues and shower divine teaching upon those subject to you: therefore rejoice, that is, conceive great joy because of the victory won in your hearts, because you have conquered the accuser of the human race. Rejoice also, you lesser ones, “who dwell in them,” that is, under the protection and discipline of those greater ones, because with them you have likewise overcome the same ancient enemy. The angelic voice continues: “Woe,” that is, misery, pain, and captivity, is upon you, “earth,” namely you who love earthly things, “and sea,” that is, you who are tossed about and embitter God by evil works. This is because the devil, having fallen from the power which he had over your brethren, “has come down to you,” that is, to your detriment [Col. 0367C], having great wrath at his lost power. The most cruel dragon exercises this wrath upon you, knowing that “he has a short time”: namely, that he will be allowed to exercise this power for only a little while, but after a little while will be tormented in hell along with you.

VERS. 13.—“And when the dragon saw that he had been cast down to earth,” namely among those who are devoted only to earthly pleasures, “he persecuted the woman,” that is, the Church, “who brought forth the male child,” namely Christ, strong and invincible in overthrowing the devil. And because the dragon persecuted the woman,

VERS. 14.—“There were given by the Lord to the woman,” that is, to the Church, so that she might resist the dragon persecuting [Col. 0367D] her, “two great wings of an eagle,” namely charity, containing in itself love of God and neighbour. Thus the Church became a great eagle, flying most high by speaking of divinity and seeing most keenly the sun, that is, the brightness of the divine essence. Therefore two wings were given to the woman, that is, the Church, “that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place,” that is, into her security, where—in that security—she “is fed,” and nourished there by the Lord with that bread, namely the preaching delivered by Christ, “for a time,” that is, one year, “and times,” that is, two years, “and half a time,” that is, half a year: namely three and a half years [Col. 0368A], during which the Lord, while present in the world, preached. And this was “from the face of the serpent,” that is, because of the present assault and pressing attack of the devil, who bites secretly like a serpent. And when the dragon saw that he could not harm the woman,

VERS. 15.—“He cast out from his mouth,” that is, from his suggestion or from his members, through whom he speaks, “water,” namely an overwhelming persecution, “like a river,” great and impetuous, “after the woman,” that is, after the Church, so that he might cause her to be dragged back from her purpose by that great river, that is, by that great persecution. But not even thus could the dragon draw away the woman, for

VERS. 16.—“The earth,” that is, Christ, who is the strong and immovable foundation of the Church and who also has a body from the common earth of the human race, “helped the woman,” namely the Church. [Note: [Col. 0367D] Add here: “and the earth.”] This same Christ “opened his mouth,” that is, his preaching: he gave his disciples the grace of preaching; or he opened the sign of his mercy, “and swallowed,” that is, destroyed, “the river which the dragon cast out from his mouth,” that is, the persecution which the devil sent against the Church through his members [Col. 0368B].

VERS. 17.—“And the dragon was angry with the woman,” that is, against the Church, “and went away,” namely withdrew far from her, in order to make war with the rest of the seed of that same Church, “who keep the commandments of God and have faith through testimony,” that is, through preaching which testifies that Jesus Christ [Col. 0368C] is God and man.

VERS. 18.—“And he stood upon the sand of the sea,” that is, upon the barren, fruitless, and dry persons of the world.

## CHAPTER XIII

VERS. 1.—“And I saw a certain beast ascending out of the sea,” that is, Antichrist with the rulers of this age, their subjects, and their ministers; ascending, that is, exalting and raising himself, “out of the sea,” namely from evil persons who embitter, that is, provoke, God; “having seven heads,” namely all the rulers of the world, “and ten horns,” that is, lesser evil persons through whom the rulers attack those who keep the ten commandments; “and upon its horns ten diadems,” namely victories over those keeping [Col. 0368D] the ten commandments, because they will seem to have conquered them by killing them. “And upon the heads of the beast,” that is, upon the rulers of the world, “I saw names of blasphemy written”: namely, I saw them blaspheming God expressly, saying that Christ was not true God, and things like this.

VERS. 2.—“And the beast which I saw was like a leopard,” that is, it was full of diverse heresies, just as a leopard is variegated; “and its feet,” namely its inferior heretics, the members of the same beast, that is, of Antichrist, were as capable in persecution and as ready to tear the faithful as a bear’s feet; “and its mouth,” namely its speech, instilled terror into the faithful as the voice and [Col. 0369A] roar of a lion terrify other animals. “And the dragon,” that is, the devil, “gave to his beast,” namely Antichrist, “his own power”; and just as he is strong and evil, so he made it evil and strong; and he gave it his authority to overthrow the faithful.

VERS. 3.—“And I saw one of the heads of the beast,” that is, one of its rulers, greater than the other rulers—namely Antichrist—“as though slain,” namely as though passing into a real death: his disciples, lying, will pretend that he was truly killed and rose on the third day. “I saw him,” he says, “as though slain unto death, and his deadly wound healed”: that is, he who is said to have died from the wound was healed; he will falsely be said to have been raised. And at this false resurrection “the whole earth,” that is, all those loving earthly things, will greatly marvel [Col. 0369B] and go after the beast, namely Antichrist, who lives beast-like.

VERS. 4.—“And they worshipped the dragon,” that is, the devil, because he gave that beast power to do what it desired; thinking that they worshipped God and that Antichrist had this power from God rather than from the devil. And they not only worshipped the dragon, that is, the devil, in this way, but also worshipped the beast itself, saying: “Who is, or was, or shall be like this beast?” Yet some wish to attack it; but who can fight against it? Meanwhile, dearest brethren, it should be noted that these things, narrated as though already past, are still to come in the last times. It follows:

[Col. 0369C] VERS. 5.—“And there was given to this beast,” that is, to Antichrist, by the Lord through the devil—that is, permitted—“a mouth speaking great things,” because he will say that he is the Son of God, “and a mouth speaking blasphemies,” because he will say that Christ, the Son of God and of the Virgin who redeemed the world, was some magician. “And authority was given to it to act for forty” [Note: [Col. 0369D] Add: “two.”] “months,” that is, to do all these things for forty-two months, namely three and a half years. Accordingly the beast, that is, Antichrist,

VERS. 6.—“Opened its mouth” by proceeding from blasphemy to blasphemy “against God,” because it will say that it is the Son of God and will say openly that the devil, who will be its father, is God. Thus it will open its mouth “to blaspheme the name” of almighty [Col. 0369D] “God,” because it will claim to be righteous, merciful, and almighty; this is to blaspheme the name of God and “his tabernacle,” that is, the humanity of Christ, by saying that he, true God and true man, was a magician. It will also blaspheme “those who dwell in heaven,” that is, in the Church, by calling them deluded and foolish.

VERS. 7.—It was also given to that beast, namely Antichrist—it was granted by God through the devil—to make war with the saints and overcome them: some spiritually, others only by bodily death. Authority was also given to it over every tribe, every people, every tongue—namely Hebrew, Greek, Latin [Col. 0370A], and other languages, because many more languages are often comprised in a single people—and every nation, generally, namely over Asia, Europe, and Africa.

VERS. 8.—“And all who dwell upon the earth worshipped the aforesaid beast,” that is, Antichrist: namely those founded in earthly things, “whose names are written in the book of life,” that is, in the memory of God and of the Lamb, who was slain for us “from the foundation of the world,” by predestination.

VERS. 9.—“He who has ears,” that is, spiritual understanding, “let him hear”: namely, let him understand that everyone who

VERS. 10.—“Leads captivity”—namely, who leads others who are upright and live well captive from the true way into a false path by depraved teaching—“shall go into captivity,” namely into eternal death. And whoever kills faithful persons “with the material sword must be killed by the sword,” that is, by the divine sentence. This is the patience and faith of the saints: namely, because tribulations and persecutors will remain for a short time and go into eternal captivity, whereas those persevering in faith will be crowned with eternal blessedness [Col. 0370B].

VERS. 11.—“And besides these things I saw another beast ascending out of the earth,” that is, the preachers and disciples of Antichrist, raised and lifted from earth into pride. And that beast “had two horns,” not in reality, but “like the two horns of the Lamb,” that is, Christ; by these are signified Antichrist’s bestial apostles, who say that they are innocent and perform miracles as Christ did, while they are rather sinners and possessed by demons. “And it spoke,” instilling terror, just as a dragon terrifies all birds by its cry [Col. 0370C].

VERS. 12.—“And it had all the authority of the former beast,” that is, of Antichrist, just as the true apostles were in the favour and protection of our Lord Jesus Christ. And that second beast “made the earth,” that is, earthly rulers themselves, and all who dwell upon it—that is, lesser earthly persons subject to those rulers—the false apostles of Antichrist made them worship the first beast, namely Antichrist himself, “whose deadly wound” [Col. 0370D] “was healed,” because Antichrist is said to have been raised from a feigned death.

VERS. 13.—“And that beast,” that is, Antichrist’s disciples, “will perform great signs and miracles,” through which they will represent Antichrist himself as God; so that it “even causes fire to descend from heaven,” that is, an evil spirit, as though it were the Holy Spirit, to descend upon the earth—namely upon those given over to earthly vices and converted to its sect. And it will make them speak in every language, as the apostles made those whom they converted to the faith speak. And this will be “from heaven,” that is, from the air, in the sight of all, not secretly in a house, as the Holy Spirit descended upon the apostles in the house where they were gathered together [Col. 0371A] (Acts II), but in the sight of everyone. And through these signs and miracles, which Antichrist’s disciples will be permitted to perform at that time,

VERS. 14–15.—“They will deceive those who dwell on the earth,” telling them to make an image of the beast, that is, to make themselves conformable to Antichrist, “whose sword-wound was healed and who lived,” that is, who will be said to live again. Antichrist’s false apostles will perform this sign: they will cause an evil spirit, as though fire, to descend from the air before all who see, by which they will deceive people and confirm them in Antichrist. And this will happen so that “the image of the beast may speak,” just as those who are conformed to Antichrist will speak in every language. And that second beast, that is, those false apostles, will cause [Col. 0371B] all who have not worshipped not only the beast, that is, Antichrist, but also the image of the beast—namely those same false apostles, who will be conformed to Antichrist, their false god—to be killed.

VERS. 16.—And those false apostles will cause all, small and great, rich and poor, free and enslaved, to have a “character,” that is, the mark of their sect, “on their right hand,” namely in their action, or “upon their foreheads,” namely in open confession.

VERS. 17.—And they will cause no one to be able “to buy or sell,” that is, to give preaching or receive someone converted through preaching concerning [Col. 0371C] Antichrist, except one who has the “character,” that is, the mark of the beast, as we have said, “and the name,” namely *Teitan*, “and the number of its name,” namely six hundred and sixty-six. For that lost man will be called *Teitan*. Antichrist’s disciples will do this because at that time no one will be permitted to preach unless he has the number of Antichrist’s name—that is, unless he is perfect and has offered him, as though to God, the hundred-and-sixty-sixfold fruit. Therefore, in the number of this name,

VERS. 18.—“Wisdom must be applied,” that is, it must be considered wisely; and therefore everyone who has understanding, namely who is wise, should calculate the number of this beast. For if a foolish person calculates this number, he will immediately think him [Col. 0371D] to be God, because this number belongs to God. Wisdom must therefore be applied in calculating this number, because although this number is God’s, for a time it will belong to the utterly lost man, namely Antichrist, who will usurp it. This number consists of six hundred and sixty-six. It is the number of Jesus Christ, whose name the beast, that is, Antichrist, makes its own.

## CHAPTER XIV

Having shown the most grievous persecution which the Church suffers and will suffer under Antichrist, he also shows, for her consolation and encouragement, how great and what kind of helper she has, saying:

VERS. 1.—“I saw; and behold, the Lamb,” namely Christ sacrificed for us, “stood upon Mount Zion,” that is, he helped the holy Church, eminent in virtues [Col. 0372A] and observing and contemplating heavenly things. He stood above her because on every side he overshadowed and protected her; “and with him one hundred and forty-four thousand,” that is, virgins innumerable to us but numbered by God, most perfect, gathered from the four parts of the world by the preaching of the Holy Trinity; “having the name of the Lamb,” so that from Christ they might be called Christians, “and the name of his Father,” namely God, so that they might be called gods, “written upon their foreheads,” namely in open confession, so that it can never be erased. For him you also, dearest brethren, who have so splendid and worthy a household, ought willingly, if necessary, to suffer, so that you may be joined to those who are so illustrious among the other faithful. He again adds, saying:

[Col. 0372B] VERS. 2.—“And I heard a voice,” that is, an admonition, “coming from heaven,” that is, from the Church, “like the sound of many waters,” namely of many peoples, who run through temporal things and flow away like water; “and like the sound of great thunder,” namely striking terror, as thunder terrifies people. And the voice which I heard was like the sound of harp-players, namely those whose task is to play the harp, playing—that is, performing the office entrusted to them—not on other people’s harps but on their own. This indeed signifies holy virgins, whose office is to mortify not another’s flesh but their own. Therefore I heard the voice of virgins mortifying their own flesh,
VERS. 3.—And they were singing, that is, they were joyfully [Col. 0372C] engaged and were keeping a song: namely, integrity of mind and body, which is their greatest delight and joy. They were singing, he says, as it were a new song; that observance of integrity of mind and body was pleasing, dear, and delightful to them, just as new things are usually more delightful and dearer than old ones. But where were they singing? Not in secret, certainly, but before the throne—that is, in the presence and sight of the many faithful who are God’s throne, so that they may receive an example from them. And not only before lesser believers, but also before the four living creatures—that is, in the presence of all teachers—and before the elders, that is, the judges. And no one could sing that song—that is, no one could keep [Col. 0372D] integrity of mind and body—except those one hundred and forty-four thousand, except those virgins; namely, those who were purchased from the earth, whom Jesus Christ, God and man, purchased from earthly conduct by giving his blood as the price. Therefore, those are virgins.

VERS. 4.—They were not defiled with women by any impurity. Truly they were not defiled by any grievous sin, for they are virgins; and these follow—that is, imitate—the Lamb wherever he goes. And these such persons were purchased: that is, God chose these, so notable in dignity, out of all the rest, and as firstfruits—that is, as offerings dearer than all others—to God the Father and to the Lamb.

VERS. 5.—And no lie was found [Col. 0373A] in their mouth: no sin of speech was found in them, because, if they committed any, they repented of it so thoroughly that it was forgiven them through repentance at death. And if they sinned in any act, nevertheless they are without stain—that is, without grievous sin—because neither venial nor grievous sin is found in them at their death, since they repented perfectly.

Alternatively: truly, in the mouth—that is, in the preaching—of the one hundred and forty-four thousand there was no lie, but pure truth. For I saw that they preached without falsehood concerning our restoration: namely, that the messenger of the Father’s mercy, the angel, flew—that is, preached lofty things—and did so through himself, the heaven and middle, namely the mediator of God and men. They also preached without falsehood [Col. 0373B] that he possesses the Gospel under his own authority, so as to preach it either himself or through his servants. Having described the assault made by the two beasts, added the Lamb’s assistance, and shown the dignity of his household, he now adds an exhortation that men should eagerly join this household, and a threat that they should turn aside from the other.

VERS. 6.—“I saw,” he says, “another angel,” that is, preachers other than Christ, carrying out his office, flying—that is, withdrawing themselves from earthly things—through the midst of heaven, namely through the universal Church, which they draw with them by word and example; having an eternal Gospel—that is, preaching which, by the office entrusted to them, promises eternal goods and brings those who fulfil it to eternity. [Col. 0373C] And he had this in order to evangelize—that is, to preach—not to swine and dogs, but to those sitting upon the earth: namely, those who despise earthly things and tread them underfoot, resting from every tumult and care of the world; and over every nation, that is, over every sort of those who remain in earthly things; and over the Jewish tribe, and the barbarian tongue, and over the people, saying with a loud voice—that is, by spiritual exhortation and persuasion.

The angel flies through the midst of heaven because the preachers of the Church seek heavenly things by contemplation of mind; they do not cling to earthly things, but also invite the peoples subject to them toward heavenly things by examples and words. For Isaiah says concerning these flying preachers: [Col. 0373D] “Who are these that fly like clouds, and like doves to their windows?” (Isa. 60). They fly like clouds because, lifted above earthly desires by the wings of virtues, they rain by their words and flash with miracles. They fly to their windows like doves because, by means of what they behold outwardly, they desire nothing earthly, but continually contemplate everlasting joys. But let us hear what the angel flying through the midst of heaven says.

VERS. 7.—“Fear God” with chaste love, not the beasts mentioned above; “and give him honor” by doing good and proclaiming him rightly, so that through you he may appear glorious, “because the hour of his judgment has come.” As if he said openly: Do not fail amid tribulations, for you will not suffer for a long time. And if you fear failure, [Col. 0374A] “worship him”—that is, seek help from him—who made heaven, namely the patriarchs, prophets, and holy Church; earth, and sea, and all things in them; and the fountains of waters, namely the Gentiles, who were fountains of many transgressions. Daniel foretold of his omnipotence: “His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not be taken away, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed” (Dan. 7).

VERS. 8.—And another angel, that is, some teacher of the Church—for preachers succeed one another—followed, saying: “Fallen, fallen,” by a twofold crushing, “is Babylon, that great city”: that is, all those confounded in vices because of the multitude of their iniquities, or because of pride, fortified by their perverse doctrine. “Fallen, fallen is Babylon.” The word being placed twice signifies infinity, in which utter destruction is understood. “For the world and its desire shall pass away” (1 John 2). And she has not fallen without cause, since by the wine—that is, because by the wine of the wrath of her fornication, namely her evil doctrine, which is the cause of God’s wrath—she gave drink to all nations living as Gentiles. The wine of fornication means vices, and especially idolatry, which is a sweet draught to sinners; by it lovers of the world defile others and intoxicate them so that they may not walk in the straight path, and therefore God’s wrath is due to them. All these things were spoken without falsehood by those one hundred and forty-four thousand, that is, the preachers of the Church. The first and second angels said these things.

VERS. 9.—And the third angel followed them, [Col. 0374C] saying with a loud voice—that is, admonishing through a great warning—thus: “If anyone worships the beast,” etc. He sets forth three angels because of faith in the Holy Trinity. As if the third angel openly says to all the children of the Church: Do not become disciples of Antichrist; for if anyone worships the beast, that is, Antichrist, and his image—that is, makes imitators of him conform to himself—and receives the mark upon his forehead, namely a sign in open confession, or upon his hand, namely in action—

VERS. 10.—He too, like Babylon, shall drink of the wine of God’s wrath, that is, of eternal damnation, which is mixed with unmixed wine in the cup of his wrath, namely that which God in anger gives to drink. For whoever is not corrected by the punishment given for correction [Col. 0374D] will be punished with eternal punishment; and he shall be tormented with the fire of envy and sulphur, that is, the stench of evil action, in the sight of the holy angels rejoicing in divine justice, so that they may waste away at the sight of the splendor of the good; and before the Lamb’s countenance, namely in Christ’s presence.

VERS. 11.—And the smoke of their torments, that is, their dark torment, shall ascend for ever and ever; they will not be tormented temporarily, but it will endure eternally. And those who worshipped the beast, namely Antichrist, and his image, namely his disciples, do not—that is, will not—have rest day or night. They deservedly will be tormented eternally, since they sinned without ceasing. As if he said more openly: It is no wonder that those who worshipped Antichrist [Col. 0375A] are punished without end, since his preceding ministers also will undergo the same punishment. For, as is written in the book of blessed Job, “they shall pass from snowy waters to fiery heat” (Job 24). And if anyone received not only the image but also the mark of his name, as was said above, he shall be tormented.

In this place Origen’s error is openly destroyed: he said that after a thousand years the reprobate would return to life, while the righteous would in turn return to punishment. Otherwise the saying of Truth is false: “The wicked shall go into eternal punishment” (Matt. 25). If anyone wishes to ask why the reprobate are tormented without end for a temporal sin, it must be said that the strict judge, when he comes, will weigh not only deeds but also wills. [Col. 0375B] For the reprobate, if it were possible, would wish always to live in this life, in order never to cease sinning. Therefore they will never lack punishment, because they never wished to lack sin. And there will be no end to vengeance for one who never wished to put an end to crime. For if, as they say, the punishments of the reprobate must end, then at some point the joys of the righteous must also end. If what the Lord threatened is not true, neither is what he promised true. To this they reply: He threatened eternal punishment to sinners in order to restrain them from committing sins, because he ought to threaten his creature with eternal punishments, not inflict them. To them we answer at once: if he made false threats in order to correct them from injustice, then he also made false promises in order to summon them to righteousness. He adds again: “If anyone receives the mark of his name,” that is, Antichrist’s, “he shall be tormented.”

VERS. 12.—Here, or this, is the patience of the saints, both greater and lesser: namely, in considering so great a vengeance. I mean those saints who keep—that is, fulfil in action—the commandments concerning the twofold love of God and neighbor, and the faith of Jesus, because they confess him to be God.

VERS. 13.—And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me. This voice pertains as much to blessed John as to all believers who await the recompense of eternal blessedness. As if the angel says to blessed John: Since I have spoken of the torment and misery of the wicked, do not despair of the blessedness of the good. Rather, write these things in your heart or commit them to writing, so that they may reach posterity; for truly blessed are the dead who die in the Lord—that is, in confession of the Lord—namely when body and soul are dissolved. “From henceforth,” that is, from the present time or from the time of the resurrection, “the Spirit says”—namely, the whole Trinity, since “God is Spirit” (John 4)—“that they may rest,” that is, suffer no longer, from their labors, which they have endured until now; for their works follow them, that is, the reward of their works follows them. As though he said: While they were in the world, greater tribulations belonged to a greater crown, and thus they were thought [Col. 0376A] to have been cast off by God; but henceforth they will suffer no more.

VERS. 14.—And I saw, and behold, a white cloud, that is, the saints or the Lord’s flesh, which no stain of sin darkened; and one sitting upon the cloud, namely Christ sits above the saints, or divinity above humanity, like a son of man, because he is now impassible and immortal; having upon his head—that is, in himself or in his divinity, in the likeness of a conqueror—a golden crown, because by his wisdom he conquered the devil; and in his hand, namely in his power, a sharp sickle, that is, the judicial sentence separating evil from good. Elsewhere he calls it a sword, saying: “I came not to bring peace, but a sword” (Matt. 10), because by it the evil are separated [Col. 0376B] from the good.

VERS. 15.—And another angel came out from the temple: in this respect Christ’s servant, that is, holy men who until now had been hidden from unbelievers, namely despised, but now appear in glory, are to judge all things, with the desire that God should make a separation of good and evil. Crying with a loud voice to the one sitting upon the cloud, that is, to Christ judging upon human flesh. But let us hear what the angel coming out of the temple, that is, all the saints, says to Jesus Christ sitting upon the cloud: “Send forth your sickle,” that is, exercise judgment, by which sickle herbs of every kind are gathered. Or, “send forth your sickle,” that is, the preaching of your own people, by which [Col. 0376C] those to be saved will be separated from those to perish; “and reap,” namely gather your own, because the hour for reaping has come, that is, it is fitting, now that the number of your people has been completed, since the harvest of the earth has dried up: namely, because the wickedness of the evil has been consummated and has no further place.

VERS. 16.—And he who sat upon the cloud sent his sickle upon the earth and reaped, that is, separated the evil from the good.

VERS. 17.—And another angel, that is, the saints mentioned above, having another office, came out of the temple which is in heaven, namely from the hidden place, having himself also a sharp sickle like Christ, because the saints received this power from Christ, who is the angel of great counsel. Having shown that the saints implore God, who possesses the power [Col. 0376D] of judging, and that judgment is thus made, he shows that the saints possess the same power, and that Christ commands them to judge and they obey his command.

VERS. 18.—And another angel, namely the holy martyrs and confessors after the apostles, who preserve the condition of the Church, came out from the altar—that is, from the Church. I mean those martyrs and confessors who offer and sacrifice themselves to God. This angel has power over fire: namely, by preaching to snatch the faithful from eternal punishments, and by excommunicating to consign unbelievers to the fires of Gehenna. And he cried with a loud voice—that is, with great desire—to him who had the sharp sickle, namely the judicial sentence embracing all, saying: “O Lord, send forth your [Col. 0377A] sharp sickle, and gather the vintage,” that is, separate the clusters of the earth ripe in wickedness. [Note: [Col. 0377D] The Vulgate reads, “the clusters of the vine of the earth.”] They abound in the malice of earthly things, “because her grapes are ripe”: namely, it is time for them to be judged, because their malice is complete.

VERS. 19.—And the angel of great counsel, that is, Christ, sent his sickle upon the earth—namely, his judgment upon earthly persons—and gathered the vintage of the earth: at the saints’ request he separated the evil from the good and cast them into the great winepress of God’s wrath, that is, into hell, where many will suffer God’s wrath.

VERS. 20.—And the winepress was trodden: namely, they were placed vilely and contemptuously in hell outside the city of God, that is, outside the fellowship of the saints, because that punishment will not be purgatorial but eternal. And [Col. 0377B] blood came forth from the winepress, that is, vengeance for the martyrs became manifest, namely eternal punishment for sin, not wine to be stored in God’s cellar. Blood, I say, came forth as far as the horses’ bridles, namely as far as the very rulers of the wicked who are to be punished, that is, the devils, for one thousand six hundred stadia. By six the perfect, by one hundred the more perfect, and by one thousand the most perfect are signified.

## CHAPTER XV

In the three visions mentioned above—namely, in the revelation of the mysteries, the giving of the trumpets, and the woman’s battle against the devil—he has followed the sequence from the beginning of redemption down to the day of judgment. In the following three, however, he dwells upon the last [Col. 0377C] times. Of the matters dealt with in the preceding visions, some have been stated more fully in other divine Scriptures, while others have been spoken of little and more obscurely. In this fifth subject, therefore, there are seven angels holding bowls containing plagues, that is, the destructions of the wicked who will exist in the time of Antichrist; this destruction especially exhorts those now living to endure. He adds again:

VERS. 1.—And I saw another sign, that is, a figure signifying something else, because those signified by this sign dwell in heaven. I mean a sign great in its wondrousness and marvellous, because it is wonderful that a human being should have such power as to be able to condemn others: namely, seven angels, that is, the preachers of whom it is said, “The angels of peace wept bitterly” (Isa. 33). [Col. 0377D] They have the seven last plagues imposed upon them by God, namely every blinding and destruction of those who will exist at the time of Antichrist. Truly they will have plagues, since in them the wrath of God is consummated: for they will exercise God’s wrath upon the wicked; and truly the last plagues, because after them God will inflict no others in the world. They have seven plagues: that is, knowledge of all the Scriptures, by which the hearts of the good are wounded unto salvation, but the hearts of the impious unto damnation.

VERS. 2.—And I saw something like a glassy sea, that is, baptism, in which purity of faith is required and people are cleansed from vices; a sea, I say, mingled with fire, because the Holy Spirit is given to those [Col. 0378A] baptized in it. And I saw those who conquered the beast, that is, Antichrist, and his image, namely avoiding conformity to him, and the number of his name, because they were not thereby deceived, standing upon the glassy sea. For those truly stand who preserve intact the grace of baptism, having God’s harps, that is, mortifying their own flesh, as God commanded them or as he himself first did.

VERS. 3.—And singing the song of Moses, the servant of God, namely the old law, which is an exultation to those who understand it rightly; and the song of the Lamb, namely the New Testament, saying—that is, admonishing others—“Great,” in the first creation, “and marvellous are your works, God Almighty”; in the re-creation, “just [Col. 0378B] and true are your ways, King of the ages,” because they render to each according to merit, and true because they bring men where they promise. The ways of God are his institutions, just and true, through which we come to God, or he comes to us. He says again afterward:

VERS. 4.—“Who, then, shall not fear you, O Lord?” That is, who shall not serve you from love and magnify your name by deed and preaching? And truly they will fear you, because you alone are gracious, saving freely. And truly they will magnify you, because all nations—namely, some from every nation through faith—will come and worship in spirit and truth before you, that is, in your good pleasure; because your judgments are manifest, since believers will know from justice that you elect some and reprobate others.

VERS. 5.—And after these things I saw, and behold, the temple of the tabernacle of testimony was opened in heaven: namely, the mysteries of the Church were revealed—the Church in which the Lord dwells, which serves in honor of God, and which contains in itself the Old and New Testaments. And because the mysteries of the Church were open,

VERS. 6.—The seven angels came forth, that is, the preachers who will rebuke evildoers, having seven plagues, that is, the sevenfold Scriptures; they came out from the temple, namely the Church. And that they might be irreproachable, they were clothed in clean, white linen, that is, surrounded on every side by strength and purity, because they will be free from sins and adorned with the beauty of virtues; and girded about their breasts with golden girdles, [Col. 0378D] restraining evil thoughts and wills through charity and divine wisdom.

VERS. 7.—And one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls; and this was through Christ, who is one—that is, the head of the four evangelists—because what they will preach they will have from the institution of the former Fathers. The bowls, I say, are golden, namely lucid consciences, full of the wrath of God who lives for ever and ever, illuminated by divine wisdom. For in their teaching consist both the full salvation of the elect and the damnation of the reprobate: from it the former receive life and the latter death. Thus he made them vessels containing God’s wrath. [Col. 0379A] By the one of the four living creatures who gave the seven angels seven bowls, we may understand the order of preachers: namely the apostles and the rest, who gave bowls to their followers, that is, entrusted divine preaching to them. For they not only baptized them, but also ordained them and made them sit in their own places, as Peter did Clement, Linus, and Cletus; to these he also handed over the power of binding and loosing which he had received from the Lord, and compelled them to sit in his chair. The same happens daily when, by the laying on of hands, bishops of souls are appointed in cities. It follows:

VERS. 8.—And the temple was filled with smoke, that is, obscurity, and this from the majesty—that is, the presence—[Col. 0379B] of God and from his power. For although at that time all things will be so open to believers, they will nevertheless be closed and obscure to unbelievers; because when he closes them through faith, hope, and charity, no one opens them. And none of the reprobate could enter the temple through secular knowledge—that is, become a temple of God—unless instructed by the preaching of the seven angels, until the seven plagues of the seven angels should be completed: that is, until all preaching of the Church should end.

## CHAPTER XVI

And because no one could become a temple except through their preaching:

VERS. 1.—I heard a voice, that is, divine inspiration or admonition, great because it commands great things, [Col. 0379C] from the temple, namely from Christ, saying to the seven angels, that is, inspiring them: You who are good as far as you yourselves are concerned, advance still further in goodness, and exercise condemnation upon wicked people. Go, therefore, from contemplation for the benefit of your brethren, and pour out the seven bowls of God’s wrath; that is, expose your clear consciences against the earth, namely against those who are upon the earth. All this was spoken without falsehood by those one hundred and forty-four thousand mentioned above, who were purchased from the earth and in whose mouth no lie was found: that is, all the preachers of the Church taught their hearers how Christ admonished and how they ought to preach.

VERS. 2.—And the first angel went from the secret place [Col. 0379D] of contemplation to usefulness and poured out his bowl, that is, his pure and profound conscience, upon the earth, that is, upon his contemporaries. As if he said more plainly: the first angel, having heard Christ’s command, preached to his hearers what and how great things God did for those who lived in the first age. And there came a cruel and most grievous sore, that is, harmful and incurable blindness and damnation arising from contempt of God, upon the people who have the mark of the beast, namely Antichrist, and upon those who worshipped his image, that is, venerated the false disciples of that same Antichrist. [Col. 0380A] To some the preaching of the saints is the odor of death, and to others the odor of life; but he presents what may more greatly terrify hearers.

VERS. 3.—And the second angel, in his office, poured out his bowl upon the sea, that is, upon those who crush and persecute the saints of God and draw with themselves into the bitterness of vices all whom they can. And it became blood: namely, damnation was inflicted upon them for the blood of the saints that they shed, as that of a dead person, because they will never rise again from that damnation, namely they will never be freed from it. And every soul—that is, those consenting—who seem to live because they do not openly persecute the Church, but will be damned because of their consent, died in the sea. Those, namely, who seemed more alive, were blinded through the sea, [Col. 0380B] namely because they admitted others as a sign of their support, just as the sea receives various kinds of fish. The one hundred and forty-four thousand also taught their hearers this without falsehood: namely, the ancient teachers taught how Noah, in the second age, according to the preaching of the second angel, planted a vineyard upon leaving the ark, and how his sons began to build a tower where the confusion of tongues occurred (Gen. 9, 11).

VERS. 4.—And the third angel, treating of the third age, when the Lord commanded Abraham to be circumcised, to offer his son Isaac to him, and to leave his land and kindred—all of which the one hundred and forty-four thousand (Gen. 17, 22, 12), who represent all the Church’s preachers, [Col. 0380C] taught their contemporaries without falsehood—the third angel, then, poured out his bowl upon the rivers: namely, he fully made known the knowledge of his teaching against those who flow from vice to vice, or against philosophers, who are the source of many opinions; and upon the fountains of waters, that is, against Christ’s pseudo-apostles, who corrupt the principal Scriptures, such as the Gospel, from which spiritual teaching proceeds. And the angel’s word became blood, because these likewise will be damned for the blood which they shed bodily or spiritually, so as to frighten others away from the preaching of the third angel.

Plato [Note: [Col. 0379D] Augustine, *On Christian Doctrine*, book II, §43, maintains that Plato was contemporary with Jeremiah and instructed by him. But Augustine later retracted this in *Retractions*, book II, chapter 4, §2, and in chapter 11 of book VIII of *The City of God*, where he declares what should be held. The Benedictines’ annotations on this passage should be consulted.] learned from Jeremiah, established in Egypt, that God Almighty made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things in them; but this same Plato turned [Col. 0380D] this bowl into blood, that is, into the perversity of error, by saying that the heavenly beings, namely angels, made the remaining lesser creation. Virgil also [Note: [Col. 0380D] *Eclogue* IV.] says from Daniel’s book that four kingdoms were preordained by God, one of which is golden; but he turned this into blood when he referred these kingdoms to Saturn and Jupiter and called them the founders of those kingdoms. To such a one the apostle Paul speaks, saying: “To have the mind set on the flesh is death” (Rom. 8).

VERS. 5.—And I heard the angel of the waters, namely [Col. 0381A] of the many teachings; that is, I understood the preachers themselves, because they will perform this vengeance while attributing it not to themselves but to the Lord, and affirming that it is done justly. As if it were said more plainly: I heard the same third angel mentioned above, namely the third order of preachers, the messenger of many waters, that is, of many Scriptures, which wash souls from grievous sins and satisfy bodies just as waters satisfy thirsty souls and wash away filth, saying—that is, giving thanks to God because the blood of the saints had been shed and he wrought vengeance upon the impious. As if the third angel spoke in the person of the preachers: “O Lord, you are just even in this, you who are and who were holy.” He does not mention “who shall be,” because he understands it as near at hand; or the past is put for the three [Col. 0381B] times. “You are just, O Lord,” they say, “who have judged these things,” namely, who through us have condemned those evil persons.
