VERS. 6.—Because they shed the blood of your saints and prophets, that is, both greater and lesser persons, and you gave them blood to drink, namely eternal punishment for the shedding of blood in attaining which they delighted; that is, you permitted them to go into the desires of their own heart. For they are worthy to suffer these things.

VERS. 7.—And because disciples confirm what teachers say, I heard another angel, that is, their disciples, saying: What you say, O teachers, is true. They also turn their speech to God out of great devotion, saying: “Lord God Almighty, your judgments also are true [Col. 0381C] and just”: namely, it is just that those who shed blood should drink the vengeance for blood.

VERS. 8.—And the fourth angel poured out his bowl upon the sun, that is, upon Antichrist, who will call himself the sun of the world. And it was granted to him—that is, God permitted Antichrist—to afflict people by heat, namely by a lesser tribulation, and by fire, that is, by a greater affliction.

VERS. 9.—And people burned with great heat, namely they failed in that tribulation. Or the afflicted martyrs will afflict their torturers with the heat of anger when they prove unconquerable; and thus their enemies will burn with envy or wrath. And these unbelievers blasphemed the name of God, who has power over these plagues, because he gives to whom he wills and takes away from whom he wills; [Col. 0381D] nor did they repent, that is, they did not come to their senses. Even if they grieved in their heart, they did not dare declare it, so as to give him glory. For the person who gives God glory both accuses himself concerning his iniquities and praises God’s just judgments. On the contrary, it is the custom of the wicked to defend their own iniquities and condemn God’s judgments.

The fourth angel, as has been said, poured out his bowl because in the fourth age the Lord gave supremacy to Moses the lawgiver, commanded him to suspend the bronze serpent upon a piece of wood so that those struck might not be harmed by the bites of serpents (Num. 21), and to bring forth a stream from the rock (Exod. 17). All this the one hundred and forty-four thousand—that is, all the teachers of the Church—preached without falsehood to their contemporary hearers. In the fifth age David was anointed king [Col. 0382A] and defeated Goliath. All this the one hundred and forty-four thousand, namely the holy teachers, taught their contemporaries without falsehood (1 Sam. 16, 17).

VERS. 10.—And the fifth angel poured out his bowl upon the throne of the beast, that is, upon Antichrist and all his ministers, for the abasement of his disciples. The devil with all his members is called the beast because, whether secretly plotting or openly raging, he strives to attack the Lamb, that is, Christ’s body. And his kingdom—that is, that very throne, namely the whole body of Antichrist—became dark: all his disciples were blinded. And they chewed their tongues because of pain, that is, because of the envy they bear toward the saints: namely, [Col. 0382B] one fed upon another’s evil speech; or they publicly and openly uttered [read: “uttered,” not “endured”] blasphemies against Christ, encouraging one another to confess Antichrist and blaspheme Christ. And, persisting in their wickedness,

VERS. 11.—They blasphemed the God of heaven, saying that the Son of God and of the Virgin had been a magician, because of their pains—that is, the plagues inflicted by which they are blinded—and their wounds, which they themselves made for themselves through the chewing of their tongues; and they did not repent of their most evil works.

VERS. 12.—And the sixth angel, treating of the sixth age in which our restoration was accomplished—all of which the one hundred and forty-four thousand, that is, the teachers, [Col. 0382C] preached without falsehood to their hearers—poured out his bowl upon that great river Euphrates, that is, upon all who abound in riches or in the vice of pride. By the great river Euphrates are expressed the power of this world and the whole multitude of the wicked, against whom the holy preachers speak unceasingly. And he dried up its water: that is, they will preach that the world’s abundance will quickly dry up, because when the world ends there will be the resurrection of the faithful, so that the way may be prepared for the kings who come from the rising of the sun, namely from Christ when he begins to shine—that is, to reveal himself. They are said to come from the rising of the sun because they are called by the Lord, who is the true sun of righteousness. They are kings who govern themselves and others well, restraining the movements of their flesh by governing them.

[Col. 0382D] VERS. 13.—And I saw from the mouth of the dragon, that is, from the devil’s inspiration and from his preachers; and from the mouth of the beast, namely from Antichrist’s words; and from the mouth of the false prophet, namely from the words of Antichrist’s apostles, three unclean spirits. These are all impious persons, who because of their excessive wickedness are to be called unclean spirits; or they are the demons themselves, who suggest in others’ hearts a spirit of blasphemy, envy, and avarice. They are called three, one in the unity of wickedness into which they agree; or because one is a lying spirit, another a spirit of fornication, and another unclean, filthy in itself and never ceasing to defile others.

VERS. 14.—For they are truly unclean spirits of demons, working signs—that is, miracles—either by God’s true permission or through their own false deception, [Col. 0383A] by which the reprobate may be deceived under God’s just judgment, as were the magicians in Egypt (Exod. 7), and Simon Magus and many other heretics who, in the time of the apostles, cast out demons in Christ’s name (Acts 8). And these malign spirits go forth to the kings of the whole earth to gather them for battle against the faithful, stirring up blasphemies and persecutions against the saints, but to their own harm; for they will soon be brought to the great day of the Almighty, that is, the day of judgment.

VERS. 15.—“Behold, I come like a thief,” that is, performing the office of a thief. It is as though the Son of God and of the Virgin were plainly saying: “I take away everything they possess when I find them asleep; but I restore those who are watchful by my visitation.” For Christ comes daily as a thief when a man dies suddenly by an unforeseen death, at a time when he does not expect it [Col. 0383B]. Blessed therefore is he who watches, namely, who is concerned for his own salvation and keeps his garments: that is, the innocence received in baptism, charity, and the other virtues. Hence blessed James says [Note: [Col. 0383D] “Peter” correctly here in another manuscript.]: “Charity covers a multitude of sins” (I Pet. IV). Blessed, therefore, is he who keeps his garments, lest he rise on the day of judgment naked of virtues and the saints see the shamefulness of his sin. He keeps his garments who strives to fulfill what he promised in baptism. These are the garments of immortality and innocence of which the first man had been stripped in Paradise; but through the slain fatted calf—that is, through the Passion of the Son of God and the Virgin—he received the same garments again in baptism [Col. 0383C]. Therefore, whoever does not defile himself with graver sins preserves these garments. But if they happen to be defiled, owing to sins that obstruct him and the frailty of the flesh that compels him, he still has a second baptism by which he may be cleansed: namely, compunction and the fountain of tears. Concerning this double baptism the Psalmist says: “Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven,” namely in the baptism of first regeneration, “and whose sins have been covered” through compunction of heart (Ps. XXXI). That host, therefore, of unclean spirits and impious men will go forth to gather together the kings of the whole earth,

VERS. 16.—“And it will gather them into the place called in Hebrew Armageddon”: that is, it will make them put their confidence in Antichrist, who is a refuge [Col. 0383D] for all who wish to steal the saints’ faith, and to whom all the wicked of diverse sects will be joined. For *Ermagedon* in Hebrew means “mountain of thieves,” or “rounded mountain,” or “the co-resurrection of wicked witnesses.” Many peoples, therefore, of diverse sects will cling to Antichrist—heretics, murderers, and false brethren—who will be a mountain of false witnesses.

VERS. 17.—“And the seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air”: that is, against the aerial powers, namely against the devils, whose dwelling is the air. And a great voice went forth—that is, it came openly—a voice making a great announcement, from the temple, that is, from the Church [Col. 0384A], from the throne, because the Church received this voice from God, saying: “It is done,” that is, all things are completed: the end of the world is at hand, the reign of Antichrist has ended, and the condemnation of the reprobate is complete. He is called the seventh angel on account of the seventh state, which will be in the time of Enoch and Elijah. Having shown over whom those seven angels poured out their bowls, he now adds what will happen to those wicked persons through the pouring out of these seven bowls: namely, that here they will oppose the good as far as they can, as though they had received an increase of malice from that very outpouring; but at last they will be cast down into hell.

VERS. 18.—“And there were,” from the disciples of Antichrist in opposition to the good, “lightnings,” that is, miracles; “and voices,” flattering words to deceive the good; “and thunders,” namely threats; “and a great earthquake,” namely one of wicked men, so grievous, such as and as great as there never was from the time when good and rational men began to exist upon earth—that is, from the time when they began to despise earthly things, from the time of Abel, who first trod the earth, that is, despised earthly things, and when the Church began to be built: such an earthquake, that is, so shameful and so violent, so great, namely so severe against the faithful [Col. 0384B].

VERS. 19.—“And the great city was divided,” that is, the entire gathering of the reprobate, because of the enormity of its crimes, “into three parts”: namely, Jews, Gentiles [Col. 0384C], and heretics. “And the cities of the nations fell”: that is, every gathering of the wicked who remain in the first generation will be condemned. On account, therefore, of this condemnation and the sins which they add, that city itself was condemned, and punishment was apportioned to each according to merit: to Jews, Gentiles, and false Christians. From the beginning of the world to the end of the age, two cities appear to be built: one of God, the other of the devil. One began with righteous Abel and extends to the last elect person; the other took its beginning from impious Cain and will end in the last of the reprobate. But here, that is, in the present age, the great city means the city of the devil. And great Babylon—that is, that great, confused collection of evildoers—came [Col. 0384D] into remembrance before God, namely into God’s presence: he remembered each of their sins, though he had previously seemed to have forgotten them, “to give her the cup of the wine of the indignation of his wrath”: namely, so that God might give that most wicked gathering a measured punishment proceeding from him as indignant and wrathful, for the pleasures it had enjoyed in the world.

VERS. 20.—“And every island fled, and the mountains were not found”: namely, all those afflicted in the world for God’s sake, and eminent in virtues, avoided in their life the fellowship of the impious in view of these punishments; and therefore they were not found among their punishments.

VERS. 21.—“And great hail, like a talent in weight, descended [Col. 0385A] from heaven upon men.” The greater talent weighs one hundred and twenty pounds, the middle talent seventy-two, and the lesser fifty. Here, therefore, he speaks of the middle talent, which consists of seventy-two pounds, because sinners in the seventy-two languages will not escape this vengeance. Great hail, heavy like a talent, signifies eternal punishment crushing sinners without end, yet with measure, because God, the righteous Judge, gives to each according to his works. And those suffering men, placed in hell, blasphemed God, calling him unjust and cruel because of the plague of hail, “for it was exceedingly great.” And those wretches, although they know that they are punished according to their desert, will nevertheless grieve that God possesses such great power as to inflict this plague upon them [Col. 0385B].

## CHAPTER XVII

Having shown the plagues of the devil and the beast, and the deliverance of the woman, lest God’s judgment seem unjust, he begins to show the just causes of their condemnation, so that the faithful may guard themselves against these causes.

VERS. 1.—“And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying: ‘Come, I will show you the condemnation of the great harlot.’” This angel represents the Son of God, teaching and speaking with John, who is truly the head of the seven angels. Having described the plagues which preachers will inflict in the time of Antichrist, and the eternal condemnation which the impious will consequently suffer, he warns them to consider the causes of that condemnation. It is as though he said: “I have shown you what will happen in that future time; and you who are present now, beware, because the same devil who will then deceive so openly deceives daily in secret, and, if he can, will lead you to the same destruction as them.” “Come,” says the angel, “O John, through understanding, and I will show you the condemnation of the great harlot”: that is, the cause of the condemnation of the wicked, who, having abandoned their Creator, commit fornication with the devil by worshipping idols and loving earthly things. She sits upon many waters, that is, reigns over many peoples, whom she draws to herself through lust. Hence the Lord says to Job: “His strength,” namely that of the devil, “is in his loins,” when he deceives men whose seed is in their loins (Job XL). Therefore the prophet speaks to Jerusalem as though to a harlot, saying: “On the day of your birth,” that is, in this age of the world, “your navel was not cut” (Ezek. XVI) [Col. 0385D], namely, you did not restrain lust.

VERS. 2.—“With whom the kings of the earth committed fornication”: that is, the princes of the age, by desiring earthly honors and pleasures of the flesh and pursuing impurity. “And those who dwell upon the earth were made drunk with the wine of her prostitution,” that is, with her manifest fornication. As a drunken man fears nothing, so those who cling to earthly things will be so blinded by love of the earth that they neither love God nor fear the punishments of hell. This great harlot is Antichrist and the wicked who will exist in his time. She already sits upon the waters, that is, already rules over wicked persons now living; and in the last time [Col. 0386A] she will rule over future wicked persons, of whom he is the head. It follows:

VERS. 3.—“And he carried me away in the Spirit into the wilderness,” that is, into the hearts of the reprobate, empty through the absence of divinity. Blessed John saw all these things not bodily but in spirit and by the understanding of the mind. In sacred language, “wilderness” sometimes signifies heaven, as in the Gospel: “He left the ninety-nine sheep in the wilderness,” that is, in heaven (Luke XV). Sometimes it signifies the minds of the saints, as is read in the Psalm: “Behold, I fled far away and remained in solitude” (Ps. LIV), that is, in the secrecy of the mind. Sometimes it signifies God, as Jeremiah says: “Who will give me a wilderness of diverse travelers?” (Jer. IX). Sometimes it signifies the hearts of the reprobate, as in Jeremiah: “How does the city, full of people, sit alone?” (Lam. I) [Col. 0386B]. “Alone,” that is, without God. Thus John also says: “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Make straight the way of the Lord” (Matt. III). For those whom almighty God does not inhabit by grace are rightly called a wilderness.

He adds again, saying: “And I saw a woman upon a scarlet beast”: that is, those wicked persons who are conformed to Eve, from whom sin began; who have the devil as their foundation, who is bloody in himself and in his own, either because they shed the blood of the saints; “full of names of blasphemy,” either because they interpret the words of the Lord wrongly and utter them falsely, or because they say that the evil things they do do not displease God; “the beast,” I say, “having seven heads,” that is, the five senses of the flesh, the error of heretics, and finally [Col. 0386C] Antichrist, through which seven the devil leads men into sin; “and ten horns,” namely, the ten kingdoms that will exist in the time of Antichrist, which are signified by the ten horns.

VERS. 4.—“And by that such beast,” that is, by the devil, “the woman was clothed in purple.” Those soft and fornicating persons, upon the devil, were clothed in purple, adorned with royal garments of earthly riches in order to deceive the faithful; and she was clothed in scarlet, because they are bloodthirsty like their father the devil, for they will kill those unwilling to comply with them. “And she was gilded with gold,” because they will seem to be enlightened by divine wisdom; “and with a precious stone,” namely the carbuncle, that is, the charity which they will say they possess [Col. 0386D]; “and pearls,” that is, other virtues; “having in her hand a golden cup,” namely divine Scripture, with which the faithful are given drink for salvation. They have it in their hand, that is, in corrupt interpretations: I mean a people full of abomination and the impurity of her fornication, things which, according to those interpretations, ought to be rejected by the faithful because they teach impurity of the flesh and fornication away from God.

VERS. 5.—And although the woman, namely that very gathering of the wicked, is so skillful at deceiving, nevertheless, O faithful of Christ, do not despair: for upon her forehead, that is, openly, she has a name written: “Mystery,” namely an unchangeably set and unknowable sign, except to the wise. To the unlearned this name is a mystery: namely that she [Col. 0387A] will be called “great Babylon,” that is, great confusion, “and mother of fornications,” namely of those departing from God and giving others an example of sinning, “and of the abominations of the earth,” on account of which earthly people will be driven away from the salvation of the faithful.

VERS. 6.—“And I saw the same woman,” as I said, adorned with diverse garments, that is, wrapped in diverse vices and consequently condemned for sin; “and drunk with the blood of the saints,” namely, so overwhelmed by vengeance for shedding blood that, through excessive pains, she does not know where she is; “and with the blood of Jesus’ martyrs,” namely those who do not fear to testify that Christ is true God and man. “And I wondered, when I saw her, with great astonishment.” Here blessed John represents those who, when they see the wicked exalted in the world, wonder when they hear the punishments promised to those wicked persons: if they are to be punished thus, why does God permit them to be exalted? But those who wonder at such things are taught to understand that this exaltation is given for greater blindness, and that eternal condemnation is consequently justly imposed [Col. 0387B].

VERS. 7.—“And the angel said to me,” that is, God inspired me: “Why do you wonder, O John?” It is as though he said: “Do not wonder, but understand what it is. And I will tell you,” that is, disclose to you so that you may understand, “the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her”: namely, why these wicked persons are punished, and the devil who caused them to sin. I mean the mystery that is unknown not to the instructed, but to the uninstructed. “The beast has [Col. 0387C] seven heads and ten horns.”

VERS. 8.—“The beast which you saw,” that is, the devil, who makes men beastlike, “was” before Christ’s coming, having dominion; “and is not,” because when Christ was born he lost his right; “and is about to ascend from the abyss,” namely from the mass of unbelievers, having dominion, because in the time of Antichrist he will receive power, that is, he will have a place in wicked men; “and he will go into destruction,” because after Antichrist’s death, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth (II Thess. II), the devil will no longer have a place on earth. “And the inhabitants of the earth,” namely the wicked, “will wonder”: when they see the power of the devil and Antichrist so annihilated, they will grieve—not as repentant persons, but merely in astonishment [Col. 0387D]—whose names are not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, although in presumption they write themselves there, saying: “I shall never be moved” (Ps. XXIX), when they see the beast that was, namely that ruled the human race, and now is no longer so dominant.

VERS. 9.—“And here,” that is, in this place, “is the mind”: that is, understanding must be applied—not by foolish and ignorant persons, but one who has wisdom ought here to exercise his understanding. It is as though he said more plainly: “In view of this punishment, you can guard yourselves.” Here, that is, in considering these matters or in expounding what follows, blessed John makes his hearers attentive. “The seven heads of this beast are seven mountains”: that is, seven dominations through the seven [Col. 0388A] states of the Church from the Lord’s advent to the day of judgment; or the seven principal vices, because through these seven the devil raises men into pride. On them the unbelieving rest, upon whom the woman sits—namely the soft, fornicating, and sin-prone—and “they are seven kings.”

VERS. 10.—“Five have fallen; one is; and another has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain a short time.” He makes the six ages of the world, with the seventh state of Antichrist added, into seven kings seated upon seven mountains. These kings, therefore, already reign in grandfathers and great-grandfathers, that is, in those like themselves. The other, that is, the seventh king, is called Antichrist, whose kingdom will not continue except for three and a half years. He is called the seventh not with regard to the ages of the world, which are only six, but with regard to the seven states, in the seventh of which Antichrist will come; and that seventh state is contained within the sixth age, which is from the Lord’s advent until the day of judgment.

If Adam had persevered in obedience, he would have made use of none of the bodily senses for pleasure; but through sin they were so corrupted that it is now natural to seek things soft to the touch, savory to the taste, melodious to the hearing, fragrant to the smell, and beautiful to the sight. These are the five kings through whom the devil rules men in childhood, because he was the cause why they were corrupted. These are the five husbands of the Samaritan woman, whom error succeeds; for after a person comes to discernment, if he sins, he is no longer said to sin through the five senses but through error [Col. 0388C]. Concerning this the Lord said to the Samaritan woman: “He whom you now have is not your husband” (John IV). The other king, called the seventh, is Antichrist, who, as was said, has not yet come; through him, more than through the five senses or through error, he will rule that same woman—that is, the entire collection of the wicked—unto eternal condemnation.

VERS. 11.—“And the beast,” that is, the devil, which was before the Lord’s advent, having dominion, and now is not so dominant, “is itself the eighth,” because his dominion extends to the resurrection, which is the eighth age. And that beast itself, namely the devil, “is of the seven,” because he similarly sins and similarly [Col. 0388D] will be punished; “and is the eighth, and goes into destruction,” he, the head of all wickedness, with his members, because he surpasses all both in evil and in punishment.

VERS. 12.—“And the ten horns which you saw are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom.” In the time of Antichrist, as Daniel says, there will be ten kingdoms, whose kings are represented by the horns (Dan. VII). But who are these Persian kings? Namely, Saracens, Vandals, Goths, Lombards, Burgundians, Franks, Hungarians, Alamanni, and Suevi; yet in the time of blessed John they had not received a kingdom. But they will receive authority for one hour as not true kings but tyrants, after the beast, that is, second after their head. It is as though he said more plainly: O faithful of Christ, you ought not therefore to fear, because however long the kingdom of the wicked endures, compared with eternity it is nothing [Col. 0389A].

VERS. 13.—All these kings, materially conquered by Antichrist in war by force, have—that is, will have—one purpose: to deny Christ and believe in Antichrist. Namely, they will hand over to the beast the strength which they have in themselves and the authority which they have over others, because they will attribute every thanksgiving to him.

VERS. 14.—All these, in word and deed, in order to subject the faithful to themselves, will fight “with the Lamb,” that is, against the Lamb. But their plan will be futile, because the Lamb will conquer them, making his own steadfast and condemning the impious with their head, the devil. The Lamb’s innocence will destroy the counsel of the beast, that is, of the devil [Col. 0389B]; for “the Lord scatters the counsels of the nations, and rejects the thoughts of peoples, and rejects the counsels of princes” (Ps. XXXII). Why? Because he is “Lord of lords and King of kings,” using even the wicked for the advantage of the faithful. And therefore he will conquer the aforesaid kings, because those who are with him are called through preachers, chosen from eternity, and faithful in carrying out righteous works.

VERS. 15.—“And the angel said to me: O John, the waters [read: water] which you saw, where the harlot sits,” that is, where Antichrist already reigns mystically, “are peoples, nations, and languages”: namely, the present wicked, gathered from every diversity of humankind.

VERS. 16.—“And the ten horns which you saw upon the beast,” namely the princes of Hebrews, Greeks, Latins [Col. 0389C], and Saracens attacking the Ten Commandments of the Law, “will hate the harlot,” namely idolatrous fornication. That is, the reprobate will hate themselves; for “he who loves iniquity hates his own soul” (Ps. X). For in the very respect in which the reprobate love themselves by following their desires, they are proved to hate themselves. “And they will make her desolate,” namely at the hands of those over whom she will rule; for the devil’s consolation is the destruction of the wicked, and he will lose that consolation when the number of the elect is complete. “And they will make her naked,” namely, stripping her of her former power. The devil has the power of working signs for deception; he will lose it when the number of the good is complete, because afterward temptation will have no place. When the devil and Antichrist, his son, have lost the power which they possessed to deceive [Col. 0389D] the human race, the reprobate will say: “Behold, how the servants of Jesus Christ have been counted among the sons of God, and their lot is among the saints. We fools considered their life madness and their end without honor” (Wis. V).

“And they will eat her flesh,” that is, they will destroy and lay bare the pleasures of the devil, Antichrist, and all their disciples; and they will hand over to torments the devil himself and his body, namely Antichrist and his members. “And they will burn the harlot-beast with fire,” that is, the devil himself, who made them commit fornication; for together with them and on account of their sins the devil himself, who incited them to sin, will be punished. Or they themselves are the flesh, because they will always be fed on punishments, and worms will always consume them [Col. 0390A], and they will never arrive at an end, although they continually fail. Therefore, while by their iniquities and corrupt pleasures, like so much wood, they kindle the fire by which they will be burned, they burn themselves. For in customary speech the reprobate are said to do what happens to them; just as we say that a man killed himself when, though able, he did not avoid mortal danger, or that he burned himself when of his own will he cast himself headlong into fire. Isaiah says of the reprobate: “Their fire shall not be quenched, and their worm shall not die” (Isa. LXVI). It will therefore rightly happen to the beast, that is, to the devil and his members, because God blinded them for their evil deserts. For God, angered by men’s preceding sins, often permits them to do that by which they offend him still more [Col. 0390B].

VERS. 17.—God therefore gave it into the hearts of those kings mentioned above to do what was pleasing to him—that is, what was permitted by God—namely, to give their kingdom to the beast: that is, to permit themselves, having been turned over to a reprobate mind, to be ruled by the devil, until they are consummated, that is, until the words of God concerning the promise of rewards or punishments are fulfilled in deed. Because above the angel had spoken obscurely about that woman, he now speaks more plainly of her to John, saying:

VERS. 18.—“And the woman whom you saw,” that is, whom I showed you above, “is the great city,” namely the multitude of the wicked, “which has dominion over the kings [Col. 0390C] of the earth”: that is, which has enticed to itself earthly, not spiritual, kings, and they especially take pride in this.

## CHAPTER XVIII

In this sixth vision he treats of the final punishments which the impious will suffer in hell for individual sins: first he shows them concerning Babylon, afterward concerning the beast and the false prophets, and finally concerning the devil himself, in whom the end is evident. He says that this condemnation has been proclaimed by Christ, who will carry it out, so that it may be believed more firmly.

VERS. 1.—“And after these things,” he says, namely after the things preached by those one hundred forty-four thousand, that is, by all teachers of the Old and New Testaments, “I saw another angel,” namely Christ, according to the preaching of those same one hundred forty-four thousand, descending [Col. 0390D] from heaven—that is, from equality with the Father—into the Virgin’s womb, having great power with that same Father according to divinity and also according to humanity. Hence he himself says in the Gospel: “All power has been given to me in heaven and on earth” (Matt. XXVIII). And the earth, namely the Church, was enlightened, the darkness of ignorance having been expelled, by his glory, that is, by his glorious preaching.

VERS. 2.—“And he cried out,” that is, he preached, “with a mighty voice,” which what he said will not lack in fulfillment, saying: “Fallen, fallen is great Babylon.” It is said twice because of the double condemnation, namely of soul and body; or because she will be punished eternally. Hence the Psalmist says: “You cast them down while they were being lifted up” (Ps. LXXII). And therefore she will fall, because she “has become a dwelling-place of demons,” that is, a gathering, because demons will dwell in her, God having been expelled by her; “and a prison of every unclean spirit,” because she keeps herself for the devil, or the devil keeps her for himself; “and a prison of every unclean bird,” namely because demons in corrupt hearts are unclean through the enticements of the flesh, and birds through the exaltation of the mind, because they move about through this air. And these things will happen to her for this reason:

VERS. 3.—“Because all nations have drunk of the wrath [Note: [Col. 0391D] The Vulgate has: ‘of the wine of wrath.’] of her fornication,” namely of the fornication by which God is angered; “and the kings of the earth,” that is, the princes of the age, “have committed fornication with her; and the merchants of the earth,” namely those who sell their souls through ambition for [Col. 0391B] secular things, “have become rich through the power of her luxuries”: that is, through the ambition of worldly pomp, namely through the sins by which riches are acquired; for every rich man either is unjust or is the heir of an unjust man.

VERS. 4.—“And I heard another voice from heaven saying,” that is, divine inspiration, or the preaching of Christ or of his own, declaring that future condemnation as present and therefore warning those now living to guard themselves: “Come out of her, my people,” that is, do not perform her works; “and do not share in her sins,” namely, do not give consent to those who commit them; “and do not receive of her plagues.” For if you are unlike them in life, you will not be like them in punishment [Col. 0391C], because only a short time remains in which they will receive the torments of vengeance according to their desert.

VERS. 5.—“For her sins have reached unto heaven,” that is, unto contempt of God through impenitence; “and the Lord has remembered her iniquities,” although he seemed to have forgotten while he permitted her to prosper. For God seems to consign to forgetfulness the good deeds of the righteous and the perverse acts of the impious when he allows the former to be afflicted and the latter to flourish in honors and dignities. It follows:

VERS. 6.—“Render to her as she herself has rendered to you”: that is, as she exercised my vengeance upon you who are being purified, so avenge my injury upon them. “And double double things according to her works”: namely, inflict greater punishments upon them, upon soul and body [Col. 0391D], than they inflicted upon you, according as they sinned against God, themselves, and you. “In the cup in which she mixed, mix for her double”: that is, as they inflicted torments upon you, so you upon them by your judgment.

VERS. 7.—“As much as she glorified,” that is, exalted herself and became proud, “and as much as she was in luxury,” namely, as much as she delighted in earthly pleasures, “give her so much torment in body and mourning in soul,” both in double measure, because she says in her heart: “I sit as a queen,” as though not to be moved, namely in honor and dignity; “and I am not a widow,” because I have consolation in temporal goods; “and I shall not see mourning,” because I do not fear future evils [Col. 0392A], but joy will remain with me. And because she says this,

VERS. 8.—“Therefore in one day,” namely the day of judgment, “her plagues will come”: death, the absence of life—that is, of God—mourning, contrary to the laughter they had here, and hunger, because they will lack God, who is true refreshment; and they will be burned with everlasting fire, because God is mighty, who will judge her justly.

VERS. 9.—“And the kings of the earth will weep and mourn themselves over her”: that is, the princes of the age, who were founded upon her, will experience pain in body and soul; those who “committed fornication with her,” that is, who preferred Babylon’s love to the chaste love of God, cleaving to her and living in the world’s delights. “When they see the smoke of her burning,” that is, when their riches fail, which is a sign of eternal burning; or when they see their punishment exalted and raised beyond measure [Col. 0392B], then they will weep and mourn.

VERS. 10.—“Standing afar off,” not in body but in will, namely desiring to be far off because of fear of her torments, and saying: “Woe, woe, that great city Babylon, that mighty city!” “Woe,” namely, she will have every misery in body, and woe in soul, because she is now spread throughout the whole world owing to the multitude of the reprobate. She pretended to be strong, not in good but in persecuting the saints, whom she afflicted and killed in different ways. And truly, Babylon, you shall have woe—every misery in body and soul—“because in one hour,” that is, suddenly [Col. 0392C], “your judgment,” that is, your condemnation, “has come.”

VERS. 11.—“And the merchants of the earth,” that is, of earthly things, or evil spirits—or, literally, those who give their souls for earthly things—will weep, because they will grieve that the things in which they placed their prosperity are perishing; “and they will mourn over her, because no one will buy their merchandise any more”: that is, the temporal glory which people used to buy will perish. For they will say thus: “When all the glory of the world has perished, there will be no goods for us to buy, nor those who will buy our goods so that we may become rich by their price.” For they grieve that they will lose unwillingly in the present what they could willingly have possessed eternally.

[Col. 0392D] VERS. 12–13.—The following things pertain to the five bodily senses, by which avarice, lust, and the other vices are nourished. These four pertain to sight: merchandise of gold and silver, precious stones, and pearls. And these four to touch: merchandise of fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet. And these six to sight: every citron wood—that is, fragrant wood—and every vessel of ivory, and every vessel of precious stone, bronze, iron, and marble. And these five to smell: cinnamon, aromatics, ointment, and incense. But these individual kinds also signify the elect, whom the beast, that is, the devil, deceptively shows himself to possess [Col. 0393A], and whose loss he grieves. And these four pertain to taste: merchandise of wine, oil, fine flour, and wheat; likewise merchandise of beasts of burden, sheep, horses, carriages, slaves, and human souls, because people too are commonly sold, or when some sell sacred orders or some grace of the Holy Spirit.

VERS. 14.—“And the fruits of your soul’s desire or concupiscence,” that is, whatever superfluous things were the desires of your soul, “have departed from you, and you will find them no more,” since the glory of the world has perished.

VERS. 15.—“The merchants of these things,” that is, of the devil, and those men who became rich from her, that is, abounding in luxury and the other vices, “will stand afar off,” namely, they would by their wish stand far off if they could, because of fear of Babylon’s torments; but they will not be able to stand far off. Everything that the reprobate handle according to the five bodily senses, they mourn when it perishes, because they know how to think of nothing except the things they perceive outwardly. “They will stand afar off,” he says, weeping and mourning, and saying:

VERS. 16.—“Woe, woe, that great city Babylon!” But this is said concerning the middling persons; for the greater ones uttered the foregoing “woe,” whereas these middling persons say, “Woe, woe.” The lesser ones, however, will utter a third “woe”: “Woe, woe, that great city,” which will have woe in body and soul, “which was clothed in fine linen, purple, and scarlet,” and abounded in every glory of the world; “and was gilded with gold,” namely human wisdom [Col. 0393C], “and precious stone,” namely the solidity of virtues in human estimation, “and pearls,” that is, diverse virtues. And deservedly to that city: “Woe, woe!”

VERS. 17.—“For in one hour,” unexpectedly, “such great riches were made desolate,” that is, destroyed: the riches, namely, of such proud Babylon. “And every pilot,” that is, the greater among the lesser, “and all who sail to a distant place,” namely those who desire to acquire something certain, such as some who seek a bishopric in order to spread their false teaching throughout the world, or those whose dominions are broad; “and sailors,” that is, their associates, yet lesser persons; “and those who work on the sea,” namely the least, who pursue the world’s profits, “stood afar off,” namely, they would by their wish stand far off if they could.

[Col. 0393D] VERS. 18.—“And they cried out with all the affection of their heart,” seeing the place of her burning, namely the horror of Babylon’s punishments—that is, hell—to which she has been delivered, saying: “What thing is like this great city,” namely in misery, “which was great in pleasures and wickedness?”

VERS. 19.—“And they cast dust,” that is, late repentance or desire for earthly things, “upon their heads,” namely upon their minds, in imitation of a penitent; “and they cried out, weeping and mourning,” displaying the appearance of repentance, and saying: “Woe, woe in body and soul, great city Babylon, in which all who have ships,” that is, voyages upon the sea, “became rich from the abundance of their vices, through her prices.” And deservedly woe, because “in one hour,” that is, in the twinkling of an eye, she was made desolate. [Col. 0394A] After predicting this condemnation to the impious, he urges the faithful to rejoice, that they may agree with the divine judgment, or because, once these people are condemned, their own reward will follow.

VERS. 20.—“Rejoice over her, O heavens,” that is, heavenly creatures, and holy apostles and prophets. It is as though he said: “Those kings and merchants of the earth will weep and mourn; but you, O heavens—that is, holy apostles, prophets, and all believers who have been made heavenly from the earth—rejoice.” Not because Babylon, that is, the whole gathering of the wicked, perishes, but because God’s judgment is just and because you have escaped such things. “Rejoice,” he says, “because God has judged your judgment upon her”: namely, as she judged you unjustly, she will be condemned justly. For the punishment of the wicked is an increase of the glory of the good. [Col. 0394B] After the individual punishments have been described, the manner of condemnation is shown to blessed John. It is as though he plainly says: “What I saw predicted, I also saw how it will be fulfilled in the future.”

VERS. 21.—And a mighty angel, that is, Christ, lifted up a stone like a great millstone—that is, those whose hearts are hard, because they are turned about by worldly things—and cast it into the sea, that is, into hell, saying: “With this force,” that is, in such a manner, namely irrecoverably, “that great city Babylon shall be cast down”: namely, the notable gathering of the confused, great in sins, which is as unsteady amid earthly pleasures as a millstone. It shall be cast, I say, into hell and shall no longer be found; but their desire shall remain, because in hell there is no redemption. Since above [Col. 0394C] he had set forth only four senses, he here treats of the fifth, namely hearing.

VERS. 22.—“And the sound,” he says, “of harpists and musicians, of flute-players and trumpeters, shall no longer be heard”—that is, shall no longer be found—“in you,” because there shall no longer be any earthly pleasure. Nor merely workers in one craft, such as smiths and carpenters: rather, no craftsman of any craft shall any longer be found in you, because, once judgment has been completed, all worldly knowledge shall be destroyed. There the most delicate breads shall not be sought, because the sound of a millstone shall no longer be heard in you; or because they were so excessive that they possessed very large mills for grinding pepper.

VERS. 23.—“And the light of a lamp,” that is, of a lantern, [Col. 0394D] “shall no longer shine in you. And the voice of bridegroom and bride,” that is, the joy of weddings, “shall no longer be heard in you,” namely after the judgment. It is as though he plainly said: Whatever the kind of this world’s glory, it shall be utterly destroyed. And deservedly shall you be destroyed, O Babylon, because your merchants were the princes of the earth, that is, devils. As if he said: Because those who gave their souls for earthly things exercised an excessive power which they cannot endure, these things shall therefore no longer be heard in you. You shall also justly perish because, through your sorceries—that is, through your errors and perverse persuasions—all nations, or at least some persons from every nation, were led astray. Now he speaks to Babylon itself concerning its fall, as though grieving over its misery; now he turns to his hearers, in order to exhort the faithful. Therefore Babylon again [Col. 0395A]—that is, every collection of evildoers—shall be cast into hell, because:

VERS. 24.—“In her was found the blood of prophets and saints,” namely, blood requiring vengeance; “and of all who have been slain,” that is, killed, “on the earth.” If one wicked person kills another wicked person, the killer is not thereby excused.

## CHAPTER XIX

VERS. 1.—“After these things I heard” in my mind—that is, after this vision I understood—that the one hundred and forty-four thousand had taught their hearers without falsehood that, once judgment has taken place, all the saints will praise the Lord for the reward of the good. His phrase “after these things,” as was said above, indicates not a difference of time but an order of narration. In contrast to what was said above, “Woe, woe, woe,” concerning the condemnation of head and members, blessed John is thus shown that the saints will say “Alleluia” three times: namely, “Praise be to God the Father, and power to God the Son, and glory to the Holy Spirit.” “I heard,” he says, “as it were the loud voice of many trumpets in heaven,” namely of those who were trumpets in preaching, saying, “Alleluia”—that is, praise beyond expression in human words. We say “Alleluia” because praise belongs to our God; that is, because he has done great good things for us, and hence we ought, by antonomasia—that is, pre-eminently—to praise him. Therefore let praise belong to God the Father, and glory—that is, immortality and impassibility—and power belong to God the Son—that is, the victory by which he conquered the devil; and to the Holy Spirit. That is, praise belongs to our God, the Trinity.

[Col. 0395C] VERS. 2.—Because, in giving what he promised, his judgments are true and just, rendering to each according to merits; because he judged the great harlot, who corrupts the earth—that is, wicked persons corrupt themselves, or one another, or the holy Church—by her prostitution, that is, by lust; and he avenged the blood of his servants, demanding it from her hands.

VERS. 3.—And again they said, “Alleluia.” By this repetition we should understand eternal praise. God has avenged the blood of the saints from her hand. And her smoke—that is, her darkness and her exalted punishment—shall ascend and increase eternally, enduring unto ages of ages.

[Col. 0395D] VERS. 4.—And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshipped God seated on the throne, saying, “Amen, Alleluia.” For not only the lesser saints praised God for this condemnation, but also those greater ones who in the Church were judges and teachers of others. It is as though they said: Truly God is to be praised because he has thus punished our enemies. Or, more plainly: “Amen, Alleluia,” that is, it is true that God is thus glorious.

VERS. 5.—And a voice from the throne—that is, an exhortation from those in whom God sits—went forth for all to hear, saying: “Speak praise to our God, all his servants, and you who fear him with chaste love, small and great, who can do these things.” To speak praise to God [Col. 0396A] is to act well. The small are those who cannot penetrate the higher mysteries, nor fulfil the Lord’s counsel when he says: “Sell all that you have and give to the poor, and come, follow me” (Matt. XIX). For smallness of intellect does no harm to one whose heart and tongue are filled with the Lord’s praise.

VERS. 6.—And I heard a voice like that of a great trumpet, and like the sound of many waters, because they have been gathered from many peoples; and like the sound of great thunders, because the exultation of the saints, who say “Alleluia,” will terrify the ungodly. Having shown the joy which the saints will have at the just condemnation of the ungodly, he adds another joy of those same saints, which they will have in their salvation. It is as though they said: Previously the ungodly reigned, but we rejoice because [Col. 0396B] the Lord our God Almighty shall reign.

VERS. 7.—Therefore let us rejoice, possessing the blessedness of the soul; and let us exult, glorified in body; and let us give glory to him, reckoning that we have all things from him, because the marriage of the Lamb has come: that is, the Church has been joined to Christ, and his wife, fit to be joined to him, has made herself ready, because the Church itself has made itself worthy to be received.

VERS. 8.—And it was given to her to be able to make herself ready, and to cover herself against the heat of the world with bright and white linen, that is, with acts of justification; for the conscience of the saints is not darkened by any stains through the advance of virtues. Now the holy Church is a bride; but when she has been led to the embraces of her husband, and sees in reality what she now sees in hope, then she will be [Col. 0396C] a wife. For linen is the acts of justification of the saints (Prov. X), which are accomplished through charity, which covers a multitude of sins (I Pet. IV). Acts of justification are also accomplished through faith, as the Apostle says: “Having been justified by faith, let us have peace in the same” (Rom. V).

VERS. 9.—And the angel said to me: “Write: Blessed are those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” Having spoken of the future marriage, he invites those now present to it. It is as though he said: Blessed are those called to the supper—that is, to that heavenly and celestial banquet—in God’s foreknowledge and predestination, namely to fellowship with angels and holy human beings, where the refreshment of holy souls will be the present countenance of almighty God. It is aptly called not a banquet [Col. 0396D] but a supper, because it will be fulfilled at the end of the world. For supper remains after dinner, but after supper there is no further banquet. And he said to me: “These words are God’s,” and therefore true because they belong properly to him.

VERS. 10.—And because I, John, understood things greater than myself and was ready to obey, I fell at his feet in order to worship him. It should be noted that this same angel is said to have had feet, because, coming from heaven, he undoubtedly assumed a body from the air. And that same angel said to me: “See that you do not do this. For I am your fellow servant and a fellow servant of your brothers who have the testimony of Jesus, because whatever the prophets said bears testimony to Christ. Therefore worship God, because I, you, and your brothers have one God.” Under the old law the angel did not forbid himself to be worshipped (Gen. XVIII, XIX; [Col. 0397A] Num. XXII; Josh. V); but after the Ascension, seeing a man exalted above himself, he feared to be worshipped by a human being. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.

VERS. 11.—And I saw heaven opened, that is, mysteries revealed: that a human being can ascend to heaven and know God. As if he said more plainly: I saw those called to the marriage; I also saw that they could come, for they have a good helper and good instructors. And what did this one open? “Behold,” he says, “a white horse,” that is, the flesh of Christ bearing the Word of God into battle against the devil; and he who sat upon it, namely the divinity, was called Faithful, because he fulfils his promises; and True, because he is truth and makes others truthful; and “in righteousness he judges,” because he renders to each one his just due, and fights in his own people against the devil.

[Col. 0397B] VERS. 12.—And his eyes—that is, the gifts of the Holy Spirit or charity—were like a flame of fire, because they burn up vices, illumine hearts, and kindle them toward the love of God. And upon his head, namely in his divinity, were many diadems, because through them he himself and his own are crowned. He has a written name which no unbeliever knows, except he himself and his own through him.

VERS. 13.—And he was clothed in a garment sprinkled with blood, that is, in flesh which suffered; or in the Church, which is slain in the martyrs. And his name is called the Word of God, because through him God the Father spoke and all things were made, and through him he made himself known to the world. Of this garment Isaiah, speaking in the person of angels addressing the Lord himself, says: “Why is your clothing red [Col. 0397C] and your garments like those of one treading in a winepress?” (Isa. LXIII).

VERS. 14.—And the armies which are in heaven—that is, in the Church, namely the faithful fighting against the devil—followed, that is, imitated, him upon white horses, namely in pure bodies restrained from unlawful things and inclined to good by the spur of charity, clothed in linen, that is, righteousness, white through the increase of virtues, clean from criminal stain.

VERS. 15.—And from his mouth—that is, from his preaching—proceeds a sharp sword, namely the divine sentence cutting off the perverse thoughts of the mind and unlawful movements of the body; or the Old and New Testaments, so that with it he may strike the nations, some unto life and some unto death. And he shall rule them: the saints, namely, advancing from virtue to virtue; and punishing the wicked [Col. 0397D] with a rod of iron, that is, with inflexible justice. And he treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty; that is, by rising again he destroyed death, which an angry God inflicted upon the first man when he sinned. Or the winepress is understood as tribulation: he treads the saints set within it, that is, he enlarges them, a tribulation which God in anger inflicted upon Adam when he sinned and justly extended to his offspring; but they become wine to be placed in God’s cellar, and, when placed there, shall be wine not of wrath but of grace.

VERS. 16.—And upon his garment, that is, his humanity, and upon his thigh, namely in the human body which he received from the Virgin without male seed, to show that he had flesh from the true offspring of the earlier Fathers, there is written indelibly: “King of kings,” that is, of the saints who rule themselves and others, “and Lord of lords,” that is, of those who exercise lordship over subjects. Matthew describes his descent through kings, namely through David and his descendants. Or “King of kings” is written in the hearts of the faithful, who are his garment and children. Having shown Christ’s dignity, by which he can overcome the devil, he adds an exhortation concerning the present. It is as though he plainly said: The faithful cling to one such as this. He next says again:

VERS. 17.—And I saw—that is, I understood—that those one hundred and forty-four thousand, namely the preachers of the Old and New Testaments, had taught this to their hearers: “one angel,” that is, Elijah and Enoch preaching one and the same thing. I say, an angel standing in the sun: namely, those preachers persisting in Christ’s preaching, not in [Col. 0398B] concealment but openly before all peoples, because Christ’s glory has been spread throughout the whole world. And he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the birds—that is, to the faithful who are swift and light in the pursuit of good works and contemplate heavenly things—who fly through the midst of heaven, namely through the Catholic faith which is shared in the Church: “Come therefore, O faithful, by working well; gather together in the bond of charity in the same faith, not following diverse heresies like the wicked. Or, come from the different parts of the world to complete the supper of the great God,” that is, to God himself, who will be your refreshment:

VERS. 18.—“That you may eat flesh,” namely, that by preaching you may destroy fleshly pleasures. Alternatively: “Come, that you may eat the flesh of kings and the flesh of tribunes,” that is, that you may delight in the torment of both the greater and the lesser; “and the flesh of those strong in body, and the flesh of horses,” namely, the carnal understanding of brutish people deceived by heretics; and of others subject to them, and of those seated upon them, that is, ruling over them, namely the prelates who are leaders of heresies; “and all free persons,” that is, kings, “and slaves,” namely tribunes; “small and great,” that is, those more and less strong. And in opposition to the open preaching of Elijah and Enoch, the one hundred and forty-four thousand taught their hearers that Antichrist would come. It is as though he said: O faithful, you must be very careful that you may be able to come to [Col. 0398D] this supper of the Lamb, because unless you fight well, you will succumb to the devil, who is ready to harm you to the extent of his strength; yet you will be able to overcome him with God’s help. It follows:

VERS. 19.—And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth, that is, Antichrist and his apostles, and their armies, namely all who obey him, gathered to make war against him who sat on the horse, namely against Christ, God and man, and against his own people, and against his army, that is, against his members. And with what weapons? Namely blasphemies, tribulations, and miracles.

VERS. 20.—And the beast was seized by the greatness of God, that is, eternally punished; and with it the false prophet, namely the multitude of Antichrist’s disciples, [Col. 0399A] who, as false prophet, performed signs before Antichrist himself, by which he deceived those who believe in him, who also received the mark of the beast, that is, its faith, and who also worshipped his image, like the Jews, who will receive him with joy. These two—namely the devil and Antichrist with his disciples—were cast alive into the lake of burning fire and sulphur, so that they may live forever amid foul and dark punishments. These will suffer greater punishments than others, like those who are burned alive.

VERS. 21.—And the rest, that is, their followers, who will suffer a lesser punishment, were killed with the sword, namely by the sword of the Word of God, of him seated on the white horse, that is, upon the body without sin, which proceeds from his mouth, that is, from his preachers. [Col. 0399B] Or those who are “the rest,” namely those who are not on the side of the devil or Antichrist but have turned to God, are dead to the world and live to God. “And all the birds were satisfied with their flesh,” that is, all the saints delighted in their punishment, or in their brothers’ progress. Hence the saying: “The righteous shall see and fear; they shall laugh at him and say: Behold the man who did not make God his helper” (Ps. LI).

## CHAPTER XX

Having described the condemnation of Babylon, Antichrist, and the pseudo-apostles, he adds the condemnation of the devil himself, and sets forth the reason why, the time when, and the person who can conquer him: namely, he who in his humble coming could bind him for as long as he wished can now, having been glorified, utterly [Col. 0399C] destroy him. And lest the birds, that is, the saints and the other faithful, should be destroyed by these men’s impiety and perverse persuasion:

VERS. 1.—I saw, that is, I understood Christ descending, that is, humbling himself in the flesh and condescending to them, from heaven, namely from divine mercy, having the key of the abyss, that is, authority, and a great chain, namely an incomparable and irresistible bond, the power that binds all things, in his hand, that is, in the work of his passion and resurrection. By “abyss” he means the dark hearts of the ungodly, or the devil himself, whom the Lord permits to rage and restrains so that he may not harm as much as he desires.

[Col. 0399D] VERS. 2.—And he seized the dragon: he showed him to have sinned, when that one who was free from sin killed him. I say, the dragon, that is, the devil, strong and powerful against the human race; the ancient serpent, who from the beginning of the world deceived the first human being by fraud; who is the devil, flowing downward into himself, and Satan, namely an adversary toward others. And he bound him: he deprived him of his former dignity for a thousand years, namely from the time of his Passion until Antichrist, during which time human beings can become perfect according to their measure; because, expelled from the faithful, he began to rule more cruelly among wicked people. Hence it is read in the Gospel that he entered into the swine (Matt. VIII).

VERS. 3.—And he cast him into the abyss, that is, into the hearts [Col. 0400A] of unbelievers by his hidden judgment. The number one thousand is used to denote the perfection of a matter. Hence we read in the psalm: “The word which he commanded for a thousand generations” (Ps. CIV). Therefore, because of its perfection, this number here signifies the whole present time from the Lord’s Passion to the end of the age. He adds again, saying: “And he shut,” that is, he prohibited the freedom to go forth; “and he sealed,” he placed a seal, that is, the sign of the holy cross, upon him. This sign so overcomes the devil himself that it drives him away from the faithful, to this end: that the devil himself may perish eternally and may no longer deceive the nations—namely those who are to be saved in God’s predestination; thus the part is understood from the whole—until the thousand years are completed, that is, until Antichrist comes. It should be known that the devil was bound in Abraham and the other faithful in a manner similar to his binding in these present times; but in them the hope of the future Christ bound him, whereas in these Christ himself, having come, bound him. “After these things,” that is, after the thousand years, “he must be loosed,” because God has so ordained, “for a short time,” and therefore he is not to be feared. He must therefore be loosed in order to receive the power he had before Christ’s coming, for three and a half years. Then he will go forth to deceive the nations, because in comparison with that deception, the deception now occurring is denied to be deception. Hence blessed Ambrose says: “The devil is permitted to be loosed for a short time so that God’s power, and the devil’s weakness and impotence, may be made manifest. God’s power makes his servants strong and patient, but the devil’s weakness is conquered by girls [Col. 0400C] and little children.” And because blessed John had said that the devil would be loosed, he says that the faithful will be judges of the devil and his members, lest they despair.

VERS. 4.—And with the devil bound, namely from the time of Christ’s Passion until Antichrist, I saw thrones, that is, lesser faithful people, released and ready to obey their prelates; and the prelates sat upon them in order to judge their subjects, and this because judgment was given to them: God, namely, imposed this judgment upon them. And I saw the souls of those beheaded, who are said to be seen because of their excellence, “for the testimony of Jesus,” that is, of his humanity, “and for the word of God,” namely his divinity; and I saw those who did not worship the beast, that is, Antichrist, nor his image, [Col. 0400D] namely his apostles, and did not receive his mark upon their foreheads, that is, his sign by open confession, or upon their hands, namely in action, but overcame Antichrist; and all these lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years, that is, throughout the whole time of their life, and therefore shall judge with him. They do not live and reign only in the future, but even in this present age, from the time when they were killed, they lived and reigned with Christ. It is as though he said more plainly: I saw, in the time of this binding, namely from Christ’s Passion, when the devil was bound—I saw the Church so released for good works; and in this same time I saw those who die for Christ immediately enter into glory and never descend to hell, as Abraham [Col. 0401A] and the other prophets descended, though they were righteous. It follows:

VERS. 5.—“And the rest of the dead,” that is, those dead in soul, “did not live,” and this because they will suffer eternal punishments, “until the thousand years are completed,” namely until eternity, which will never end, is ended. “This is the first resurrection”: namely, that the soul should conquer the devil and sin and, living in a mortified body, acquire virtues, in contrast with that resurrection which will be at once in soul and body. And although not all can be perfect, nor will all possess the same brightness, nevertheless:

VERS. 6.—Blessed is the person, because he shall attain blessedness, and holy, because he shall be firm in it, who has [Col. 0401B] a share in the first resurrection. Its parts are giving alms, fasting, and cleaving to divine contemplation. And truly blessed are those in whom the first resurrection has a share, because in them the second death—that is, eternal condemnation which will be in body and soul—has no share or power, because they will be grieved in nothing. But those who do not live with Christ and do not conquer will not be blessed, but rather unhappy, because they have no share in the first resurrection. The second death is so called when body and soul are punished together. Adding again, he says: But they shall be priests of God and Christ, offering eternal praises to the Trinity, that is, to God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit; and they shall reign with him for a thousand years, namely always ruling themselves toward what is better. And they shall reign not only after the thousand years, about which there is no doubt, but even during these thousand years with the Trinity of God and with Christ’s humanity, which suffered for the salvation of the human race. But:

VERS. 7.—When the thousand years have been completed, Satan will be loosed—that is, he will receive his former power from his prison, namely from the hearts of the reprobate in which he is now bound, so that he may not rage according to his will—and he will go forth, namely exercise power, and deceive: he will lead away from Christ to himself the nations which are upon the four corners of the earth, namely Gog, which is interpreted “covered,” and Magog, which is interpreted “uncovered.” By these two peoples we understand the hidden and manifest persecutors of the Church. Their number [Col. 0401D]—that of Gog and Magog—is as infinite as the sand of the sea, and they are as barren and fruitless as the sand of the sea. Literally, he will first deceive these two nations and through them proceed to others. Some say that these nations are the Getae and Massagetae. And he will gather them for battle, not verbally but in mind.

VERS. 8.—And they ascended, namely the devil and his members, that is, Gog and Magog, swelling with pride, over the breadth of the earth, that is, throughout the whole world; and, though they will not be able to enter as if invading, they will surround the camp of the saints, that is, the saints always ready for spiritual battle, and the beloved city, namely those same saints, fortified by God with virtues and united in battle. Of this city it is said: “A city set upon a mountain cannot be hidden” [Col. 0402A] (Matt. V).

VERS. 9.—And fire came down from heaven, that is, sudden destruction, and devoured them, because they will perish swiftly. And the devil, who deceived them, was cast into the lake of fire and sulphur. Fire comes down from heaven as it were from God when envy increases in the reprobate through the preaching of the divine Word; and so the very preaching which is life to the righteous is everlasting condemnation to the reprobate. Therefore the devil was cast into the lake of fire and sulphur, where the beast is, that is, Antichrist.

VERS. 10.—And the false prophets, that is, his false prophets and disciples, shall be tormented day and night: day in relation to the glory of the righteous, and night in relation to their own punishments, unto ages of ages. [Col. 0402B] Amen. Or “day and night” is used to indicate variation in their punishments. Having described the destruction of the devil and his members, he adds the destruction of the world for the greater punishment of the ungodly. For it is fitting that, once wicked people have been destroyed, the world also should be destroyed—namely, the world’s inconveniences, insofar as it had been corrupted by them.

VERS. 11.—And I saw a throne, that is, the Church, great in multitude, white through immortality and impassibility: namely the more perfect and greater saints, who, made white, immortal, and impassible, will be God’s throne on the day of judgment. And I saw one seated upon the throne, namely Christ resting and judging in his aforementioned saints; from whose presence the earth fled, from this form, [Col. 0402C] and heaven, that is, the air, and no place, namely this condition, was any longer found for them. For the earth will no longer have mountains and valleys, nor buildings; nor will it be heavy as it now is, nor be able any longer to support bodies such as it now supports. Nor will the air any longer be now bright, now dark, now day, now night, as it is now. Hence blessed Paul says: “The form of this world passes away” (I Cor. VII). Although he had often spoken of the glorification of the saints and the punishments of the ungodly, he had made no mention of bodies, namely whether they were to be glorified or punished; this he here plainly shows.

VERS. 12.—And I saw the dead, great and small, that is, wicked persons both greater and lesser, standing [Col. 0402D] bodily before the throne, because the saints shall fully behold the merits of each person. And books were opened, namely those of the divine commandments, when they shall say: “And we fools considered their life madness: behold how they are counted among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints” (Wis. V). And another book was opened, that is, the conscience of each individual, which is that of life, namely of those who truly live. Or Christ is the book of life, who will then appear mighty to all and give life to his own. Or the book is God’s foreknowledge, because then the wicked will openly know that they were not predestined to the life which, while in the world, they promised themselves. Or the opened book is the divine commandments, because the ungodly omitted to perform them and will know themselves to be punished deservedly. Or, as we have said, the opened books are the consciences [Col. 0403A] of individuals, which will be open to all. And the dead were judged from the things written in the books: namely, by comparison with the saints the ungodly will be condemned, for they will read in them what they refused to do. Therefore they were judged according to their works, because a greater punishment will be given to some and a lesser to others.

VERS. 13.—And the sea, that is, the world, will restore to life its dead, namely the bodies of the dead that were in it. He wishes plainly to show that the bodies of the dead, wherever they have been cast, will be brought to life at that judgment. Therefore the sea, namely this world, gave up its dead, that is, the bodies of the dead that were in it. And death, that is, the devil, and hell, namely the place of darkness, gave up their dead, namely the souls [Col. 0403B] of the dead, who, or which, were in them; and judgment was rendered concerning each according to their works.

VERS. 14.—And hell, that is, those deep in vices, and death, namely the devil, were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. It is as though he plainly said: Guard yourselves against the first death, that is, sin, because this true death follows from that first one.

VERS. 15.—And whoever was not found written in the book of life, that is, predestined to eternal life, was cast into the lake of fire.

## CHAPTER XXI

In this seventh vision he treats of the renewal of the elements and the glorification of the saints, describing [Col. 0403C] the merits through which the saints are thus to be glorified.

VERS. 1.—And I saw a new heaven, that is, air having a new condition: namely, motionless, without lightning and thunder, receiving no variation of light and darkness, and cleansed of every defilement by fire which, like a flood, will rise above all mountains. Hence Master Anselm says [Note: [Col. 0403D] *Elucidarium*, book III, ch. 15]:

> “Heaven, sun, moon, stars, and waters, which now hasten in an unretarded course, as though desiring to be changed into a better state, will then remain firmly fixed and at rest, transformed by an unchangeable glorification. Heaven will put on the glory of the sun, and the sun will shine seven times more brightly than it does now. Hence the prophet Isaiah says: ‘The light of one day,’ namely of eternity, [Col. 0403D] ‘will be like the light of seven days.’ The moon and stars will be clothed in ineffable splendour (Isa. XXX). The water, however, which merited to touch Christ’s body and washed in baptism, will surpass every beauty of crystal. The earth, which cherished the Lord’s body in its bosom, will be wholly like paradise; and because it has been watered with the blood of the saints, it will be adorned forever, without fading, with fragrant flowers—namely lilies, roses, and violets. This earth, which had formerly been cursed when man sinned and subjected to thorns and thistles, will then be blessed by the Lord forever, and there will be no further labour or pain.”

Therefore the earth likewise will have a new condition. It will have, as we believe, no mountains, [Col. 0404A] forests, buildings, beasts, birds, human beings, or other such things. The world will not utterly perish; but cold and heat, hailstorms, whirlwinds, lightning, thunder, and other inconveniences will, as we believe, wholly perish. Therefore the first heaven, as has been said, and the first earth passed away: that former condition in which they previously were is no longer necessary according to the first state. “And the sea is no more,” that is, the collections of waters have already lost their former condition, in some unknown manner—whether through fire, like the other elements, or by God’s will alone. Thus it is beyond doubt that the transformation of air and earth occurs through fire; but concerning water even the holy doctors are uncertain. For, as was said above, it is believed to possess purification within itself.

[Col. 0404B] VERS. 2.—And I saw the city, that is, the Church placed in eternal peace and glory, and so fortified that neither the devil nor any persecutor will be able to harm it; I say, the holy city Jerusalem, that is, established firmly and without end in glory, presently and fully beholding eternal peace, namely God, who is peace to those who come to him; new, namely immortal and impassible; coming down from heaven, because the Church humbly understands that it has received everything it possesses by God’s grace alone; prepared by God as a bride adorned for her husband. For as a bridegroom prepares gifts for his bride before he takes her as his wife, so Christ prepares faith, virtues, and good works for the Church before he receives her into glory. Having said that he saw the renewal of the elements [Col. 0404C] and the glorification of the saints, because this was unknown and unbelievable, the author adds the authority of the holy Fathers who foretold these things.

VERS. 3.—“And I heard,” he says, “a voice”—that is, an exhortation—“great,” because it treats of secret things, “from the throne,” namely from those in whom God principally sits, saying: “Behold the dwelling of God with human beings.” That is, it is evident that human beings, according to their measure, who have imitated him and made good use of reason, will share the same glory as Christ’s humanity, in which God the Word dwells and served as a soldier. Hence he himself says in the Gospel: “Father, I will that where I am, these also may be with me” (John XVII). And as he says elsewhere: “Where the body is, there the eagles will be gathered” (Matt. XXIV). And he himself will dwell with them, not temporarily but eternally; and then they will be his people, committing no offense or sin, which cannot be so while they live in the flesh. And God himself, present to them even according to his divinity, will be with them as their God, namely because they will never sin and he will never depart from them.

VERS. 4.—And because there will be glory there and no sorrow, God will wipe away every tear from their eyes, because there will no longer be any cause that makes them weep. The first man was created in paradise under this law: if he had not sinned, he would have remained immortal and, after the number of his days was fulfilled, would have passed from that earthly paradise to the heavenly homeland without the intervention of death. But if he sinned, he could die. Therefore God will truly wipe every tear from the eyes of the righteous in the heavenly paradise, because death will be no more there, that is, no more dissolution of soul and body as in the earthly paradise; nor tears, because there will be no cause of tears; nor mourning, namely the penitential weeping for sins; nor crying out, that is, any disturbance; nor pain, namely the evil conscience of sins, will be any longer, because the former things have passed away: namely, because there is no longer a place for them, when there are no sins from which these evils, which formerly reigned, proceeded.

[Col. 0405B] VERS. 5.—And he who sat on the throne said. Having set forth the authority of the saints concerning this renewal, he also sets forth the authority of God himself, saying: “Behold, I make all things new,” namely the things mentioned above. And he said to me: O John, write, namely in your heart and in the hearts of others. Write, therefore, because these words are most trustworthy, namely fit to be believed, and they will be believed readily and quickly; and true, because they shall be fulfilled.

VERSE 6.—And he said to me: “It is done,” that is, the things which had to be completed have been completed. And lest blessed John should ask what would happen after that renewal, he is told that nothing remains to be done. As though he said: “O John, do not seek to know what will happen after the renewal of all things; for all is done. And you may know this from the fact that I am Alpha and Omega, that is, the beginning and the end.” As though he said: “I shall be able to accomplish this renewal, because all things were made through me and will be brought to completion in me. And all must hasten toward this renewal, because to him who thirsts—that is, desires—I shall give from the fountain, namely from myself, who am the source of all blessedness, water of life, because it gives life; and I shall give it freely, that is, by grace alone.”

VERSE 7.—And he who conquers, namely sins and vices, shall possess these things; that is, he shall firmly obtain the aforesaid goods. For I shall not give them to one who thirsts—that is, desires—for a time only, but to one who perseveres continually. And I shall be his God, that is, his eternal satisfaction; and he shall be my son, which above was said of the people.
